note: Use on damp skin in the shower, then rinse. Once or twice a week, body only, never on freshly shaved or broken skin.

name: Bamboo salt gargle (as posted)
note: About 3% salt, stronger than the usual gargle, so it can sting a raw throat or mouth sores. Gargle for 30 seconds and spit. For children, only once they can gargle without swallowing (usually 6 or older).

name: Gentle salt-water gargle
note: The standard strength: half a teaspoon of any salt in a cup of warm water. Gargle and spit, up to a few times a day. See a doctor if a sore throat lasts more than a week, comes with a high fever, or makes swallowing or breathing hard.

name: Calendula body butter (whipped)
claim: Heals all sorts of skin issues; gentle enough for baby bums and dog paws
note: From thewildapothecary: 4 oz calendula-infused apricot oil and 8 oz shea, melted, chilled and whipped. The infused oil is counted as apricot oil. Infuse fully dried calendula on very low heat for about 6 hours and strain well. Calendula soothes dry, chapped skin; it won't heal infected, oozing or spreading rashes, which need a doctor or vet. With no essential oils, it's a fine pick for babies and pets.

name: Kefir face and hair mask
claim: Brightens skin, soothes breakouts, glossy hair
note: A Caucasus tradition. Use plain kefir, not flavored. Leave on 10 to 15 minutes, then rinse well. It gives a soft glow from mild lactic acid; it won't treat acne.

name: Chamomile tea compress
note: Steep, cool fully, soak a clean cloth and hold it on the skin for 5 to 10 minutes. Make it fresh each time.

name: Rose water facial mist
note: Buy rose water sold for skin, with no added alcohol. Keep unpreserved rose water in the fridge and use within about a week; one with a preservative keeps as its label says. It refreshes and lightly calms; it won't replace a moisturizer.

name: Brightening whipped body butter (licorice)
note: From a TikTok recipe. The post adds "2 other oil-soluble lightening powders" without naming them, so they're left out; ask the seller what they are before buying, since unnamed lighteners are how mercury and steroids slip in. Licorice extract can gently fade marks over months; daily sunscreen matters more.

name: Lavender milk tea bath
claim: Silky, softening soak (Inoki Lavender Milk style)
note: Tie it in a muslin bag. Oats and coconut milk soften; lavender and butterfly pea add scent and colour. It won't brighten skin.

name: Rose, ginger and mugwort tea bath
claim: Soft, supple skin (Inoki Revitalizing Oasis style)
note: Muslin bag in a warm bath. Mugwort isn't for pregnancy or daisy-family allergies; ginger can tingle sensitive skin.

name: Osmanthus and jasmine tea bath
claim: Sweet floral soak (Inoki Golden Embrace style)
note: Mostly a fragrance and relaxation soak. Jasmine is a known fragrance allergen for some people.

name: Ginger, cinnamon and citrus winter bath
claim: Warming winter soak (Inoki Winter Tranquility style)
note: Use cinnamon sticks, not powder, and keep it to a short soak; cinnamon can redden sensitive skin. Dried citrus peel is fine in a bath; skip fresh peel if you'll be in the sun afterwards.

name: Amla and flax pre-poo
note: Like the Dabur Amla oil and flaxseed pre-poos in the long-hair carousel. Work through dry lengths, leave 30 to 60 minutes, then shampoo. It reduces breakage, which is how length is kept; it doesn't speed growth.

name: Rose essence toner (Stenders-style)
claim: Hydrating rose toner for the face
note: Standalone DIY of the Stenders Wild Rose toner. Mix, then add the preservative at the strength its label gives; without it, keep in the fridge and use within a week. Pat on after cleansing, before moisturizer.

name: Milk bath powder (Stenders bathing milk style)
note: Standalone DIY of the bathing milk. Stir a few spoonfuls into a warm bath. Keep the jar dry and use a dry spoon.

name: Whipped shower soufflé with sugar (Stenders-style)
note: Standalone DIY of the cranberry shower soufflé. Whip the soap and glycerin, then fold in sugar just before use or keep the jar dry. Body only.

name: Gentle rice and honey face polish
claim: A face-safe swap for the "facial scrub"
note: Fine rice flour instead of the body polish's coarse sugar and seeds. Massage softly for 30 seconds on damp skin, rinse, once or twice a week. Skip on active acne or broken skin.

name: Pomegranate and shea body polish (Dove-style)
note: Standalone DIY of the Dove pomegranate polish, kept for the body. Use on damp skin in the shower, then rinse. Not on the face or freshly shaved skin.

name: Sauna honey body mask (Stenders-style)
claim: Soft skin after a warm shower or sauna
note: Standalone DIY of the Sauna Honey Grapefruit. Spread on warm, damp skin, leave 5 minutes, massage and rinse. Grapefruit oil is kept at 0.5%, which is fine in a rinse-off; skip it if you'll be in the sun right after. Mix fresh, since honey and salt pull in water.

name: Jasmine infused body oil
note: Infuse fully dried jasmine flowers in warm oil for a few hours, then strain. Flowers left floating in the bottle look pretty but can mold if any moisture got in, so strain for anything you'll keep.

name: Cinnamon, baobab and vanilla body oil
claim: Warm fall massage oil (Lemora Cinnamon Divine style)
note: Steep one cinnamon stick for a few days, then remove it; left in the bottle it keeps releasing cinnamaldehyde, a common skin allergen. Patch test, keep it off the face and intimate areas, and skip it on sensitive skin.

name: Rosemary peppermint scalp oil
note: About 0.9% essential oil in total. Massage into the scalp before washing. Not for children under 6, and keep it away from eyes. It feels tingly and fresh; for thinning, minoxidil is the proven option.

name: Lavender bergamot massage oil
note: Use bergamot labelled FCF or bergapten-free; regular bergamot burns and darkens skin in sunlight. The calm comes from the massage and scent; it won't treat anxiety or insomnia.

name: Chamomile calm body oil
claim: Soft, soothing body oil (Lemora Chamomile Calm Energy style)
note: Matches the label: sweet almond, grapeseed, avocado and apricot oils infused with chamomile, plus vitamin E. Infuse dried flowers and strain. Daisy or ragweed allergy risk.

name: Ethereal garden pregnancy bath
note: Uses the blend in the Inoki post, with no mugwort, cinnamon or essential oils. Keep the water warm, not hot (below about 38 C), soak 10 to 15 minutes, and get out slowly, since you can feel faint. Check with your midwife or doctor if you have any concerns.

name: Beetroot cream blush (as posted)
note: From Candice's 4-ingredient blush. It works as a sheer tint. Sift the beetroot through a fine mesh, or it feels gritty. Coconut oil can clog pores on cheeks; shea is the post's own swap and a better pick for breakout-prone skin. "Toxin-free" isn't a real category: every ingredient here is safe because of its dose, not its label.

name: Beetroot cream blush (shea swap)
claim: Sheer rosy cheek and lip tint
note: The same recipe with shea instead of coconut oil, which is gentler on pores. Melt, stir in finely sifted beetroot powder, pour into a small tin and let it set.

name: Hibiscus, jasmine and rose body scrub (Cami Zawina)
note: The post doesn't give amounts for the flowers, argan or shower gel; 2 tbsp of each flower, 1 tsp argan and 2 tbsp shower gel are assumed. Blend the flowers fine. Cinnamon powder can sting and redden sensitive skin, so it's kept to 1 tsp in 2 cups of sugar; skip it on freshly shaved skin. Keep shower water out of the jar.

name: Rose water, coconut and lavender hair mist
claim: Softens dry, damaged hair; promotes growth
note: Oil and water separate, so shake before every spray, and coconut oil turns solid below 24 C and can clog the nozzle; liquid fractionated coconut or jojoba sprays better. Without a preservative, keep it in the fridge and use within a week. It softens and adds scent; it won't make hair grow faster.

name: Sea salt scalp scrub (scaler-style)
claim: Lifts buildup after protective styles (like Dr.FORHAIR Folligen, GROWUS and LABO-H sea salt scalers)
note: A DIY take on Korean scalp scalers. Massage gently into a wet scalp for a minute, then shampoo. Once a week at most. Skip it on a scratched, sore or flaking-and-raw scalp, and on fresh braids or extensions.

name: Tea tree water scalp scaler (STEAMBASE-style)
claim: Clears oil and flakes from the scalp
note: A thin pre-shampoo rinse. Part your hair, apply to the scalp with a nozzle bottle, massage 2 to 3 minutes, then shampoo. Tea tree is kept well diluted; it can irritate a scratched scalp and isn't for children under 6. Once a week.

name: Cooling mint scalp scrub (DALEAF Apple Mint-style)
note: Massage gently into a wet scalp for a minute, then rinse and shampoo. The tingle is menthol, not deep cleaning. Peppermint is kept low; keep it away from eyes and don't use it on children under 6. Skip on a sore or broken scalp.

name: Rosemary scalp scrub (AROMATICA-style)
claim: Lifts buildup with a herbal scent
note: Grind the dried rosemary fine so it rinses out. Massage softly into a wet scalp, then shampoo. It cleans and smells fresh; the hair-growth claims for rosemary come from rosemary oil, and even those are weak.

name: Gentle sugar scalp scaler (PLU / MODAMODA-style)
claim: Soft scrub for a sensitive, itchy scalp
note: The gentlest of the set: fine sugar dissolves as you massage, and aloe and glycerin keep it from feeling stripping. Once a week. The biotin in some scalers doesn't help hair grow from the outside.

name: Guava leaf vinegar shampoo (as posted)
claim: Vinegar-only hair wash that feeds the scalp microbiome
note: From Sour Flower Vinegar's comment: 1 part apple cider vinegar to 1/4 part guava leaves and a pinch of salt, blended and steeped. Used neat on the scalp, vinegar is strong enough to sting, dry hair (commenters say it felt "like hay") and irritate a broken scalp. It doesn't clean oil like a shampoo, and there's no evidence it "feeds" the scalp microbiome. Dilute it, as in the rinse below.

name: Guava leaf vinegar rinse (diluted)
claim: Shine and a clean scalp feel after shampoo
note: About 1 tablespoon of the steeped guava vinegar in a cup of water. Pour over hair after shampoo, leave a minute, rinse, then condition. Once a week. Skip on a scratched scalp.

name: Guava leaf tea hair rinse
note: Simmer a handful of leaves in water for 15 minutes, cool fully and strain. Pour over the scalp after washing; rinse or leave in. Keep leftovers in the fridge and use within 2 days. A pleasant tradition; it won't treat alopecia or sudden hair loss, which need a doctor.

name: Fresh guava leaf deodorant paste
claim: Gentle underarm deodorant for teens (Dominican tradition)
note: From a comment: crush the youngest, tenderest leaves into a paste and apply. Tannins may reduce odour a little for a few hours; it isn't an antiperspirant. Fresh paste spoils, so make it each time and patch test first.

name: Pistachio body wash (thepretty skinparlor)
note: Exactly as posted: about 0.5% fragrance, a sensible level for a wash. Use a cosmetic-grade fragrance oil and an already-preserved base. The green colour in the photo is mica or dye, not pistachio.

name: Pistachio vanilla body butter (thepretty skinparlor)
claim: Rich fall moisture with a creamy nutty scent
note: Exactly as posted; makes about a 6 oz jar. Melt the butters, stir in jojoba, chill until partly firm, whip, then add arrowroot and fragrance. Pistachio fragrance oil is a scent, not nut extract, but check the label if anyone has a nut allergy.

name: Pistachio salted caramel body oil
claim: Fast-absorbing glow oil with a sweet scent
note: A DIY take on the "ultra-luxe" oil, which lists only jojoba and vitamin E plus fragrance. It moisturizes and adds shine; the "skin barrier support" comes from the oil itself, not the scent. The salt is a scent note, so don't add real salt.

name: Pistachio and brown sugar body oil (Porter + Rose style)
note: Pair it with a plain whipped shea butter for the two-step look. Brown sugar and praline are scent notes. Skip almond oil for anyone with a nut allergy and use sunflower or jojoba.

name: Golden Hour hair perfume (as posted)
claim: Replaces your perfume; smells like designer luxury
note: From naturalpoonam: 10 drops in 2 tbsp rose water is about 1.6% essential oil, over the 1% limit for leave-in hair products, and peppermint shouldn't be used around young children. Oils float on water, so it sprays unevenly unless shaken hard, and rose water spoils without a preservative. Spray on lengths, not the scalp.

name: Golden Hour hair perfume (safer)
claim: Fresh citrus mist for hair lengths
note: Half the drops, kept under 1%. Shake before each spray, mist lengths only, and use within a week from the fridge. It won't smell like a designer perfume; it's a light, short-lived citrus scent.

name: Velvet Bloom hair perfume (safer)
note: From naturalpoonam: rose, jasmine and ylang ylang in distilled water. Jasmine and ylang ylang are common fragrance allergens, so it's trimmed to stay under 1%. Shake well and keep in the fridge. It won't smell like Chance, which is built from synthetic musks and aldehydes.

name: Midnight Moon hair perfume (safer)
claim: Woody, calming mist; "smells like Baccarat Rouge 540"
note: From naturalpoonam: lavender, frankincense and cedarwood in witch hazel. Witch hazel helps the oils mix a little, but it still needs the fridge and a week's use without a preservative. Trimmed to stay under 1%. It's a pleasant woody scent; Baccarat Rouge 540 relies on lab-made notes that essential oils can't copy.

name: Rose Garden perfume roll-on
note: From the DIY body perfumes chart, which leaves out the carrier: use about 7 drops in a 10 ml roller topped up with jojoba (the chart's 10 drops is right at the limit). Pulse points only.

name: Sunshine Glow perfume roll-on
note: From the chart. Lime is cut to 1 drop and grapefruit to 4 to stay within sun-safe limits; still wear it on covered skin or at night. Pulse points only.

name: Spicy Rose perfume roll-on (as posted)
note: From the chart. Cinnamon bark oil is one of the strongest skin sensitizers, even in a roller; swap it for a drop of clove-free vanilla or sandalwood.

name: Sacred Ground perfume roll-on
note: From the chart. Myrrh is traditionally avoided in pregnancy. Pulse points only.

name: Herbal shampoo powder (Asbat Al Jamal style)
claim: Gentle herbal wash for hair that breaks
note: Mix the dry powders and store dry. For each wash, stir 2 tbsp with warm water into a paste, massage into the scalp, leave 3 minutes, rinse well. Shikakai and reetha lather gently but sting eyes. It reduces breakage-related shedding; shedding from the root needs a doctor. The original's jojoba, vitamin E and B5 can go in a separate leave-in.

name: Japanese-style mineral body smoother
claim: Smooth elbows, knees and heels (spa salt polish)
note: From your pasted recipe. The water or green tea makes it a water-containing mix that can grow mold, so mix it fresh per use, or leave out the water and store it dry with the lid closed. Salt stings cuts and freshly shaved skin. Once or twice a week, body only.

name: Vietnamese-style coffee body scrub (Dak Lak style)
note: From your pasted recipe. Use dry grounds and keep shower water out of the jar. Leaving it on 2 to 3 minutes is fine, but caffeine doesn't brighten skin or reach deep; the glow is from exfoliation and oil. Coconut oil can clog pores on the back and chest. Body only.

name: Spicy Rose perfume roll-on (safer)
note: The chart's blend with sandalwood in place of cinnamon bark, which is a strong skin allergen. Pulse points only.

name: Mango leaf vinegar shampoo (as posted)
note: From Sour Flower Vinegar: young mango leaves blended into vinegar and used as a shampoo. Used neat, vinegar stings the scalp and dries hair, and doesn't clean like shampoo. Mangiferin hair studies are lab and animal work only. Dilute it, as in the rinse below.

name: Mango leaf vinegar rinse (diluted)
claim: Shine and a clean scalp feel
note: 1 tbsp of the steeped mango leaf vinegar in a cup of water after shampoo, rinse after a minute, then condition. Once a week. Patch test if mango skin or sap gives you a rash.

name: Saffron glow face oil (Pretty Farm Girl)
claim: Anti-aging serum that brightens and softens fine lines
note: Six oils as posted, with amounts assumed. Steep a pinch of saffron threads in the oils for a week, then strain. Sea buckthorn is deep orange and can tint skin and pillowcases, so keep it to a few drops. Coconut oil clogs pores on many faces, so jojoba replaces it here. It moisturizes and gives glow; it won't soften lines the way retinoids or sunscreen do.

name: Lavender hinoki mist (Sabbatical-style)
claim: Calming aromatherapy room and pillow mist
note: A home version of the Lavender Hinoki mist. Witch hazel helps the oils disperse; shake before each spray. Mist on pillows, linen and the room, not straight onto the face. Without a preservative it can grow mold, so keep it in the fridge and make small batches.

name: Vanilla almond cocoa body butter (DreamInfinite-style)
note: Infuse a split vanilla bean in warm almond oil for a few hours, strain, then whip with raw cocoa and shea. Raw cocoa butter adds a chocolate scent. Contains almond, so skip it with a nut allergy.

name: Sticky rice and honey face mask (brendita)
claim: Brightens, smooths, reduces acne scars, controls oil
note: Rinse the rice well, overcook it to a soft paste, cool fully, then blend with honey. The cleansing powder is optional. Use it the same day; cooked rice spoils fast and can grow bacteria. It leaves skin soft and glowy for a day. It won't fade acne scars or control oil long term; for breakouts, salicylic acid or adapalene do that.

name: Glycerin hand lotion (Corn Huskers-style)
claim: Fast-absorbing lotion for very dry, cracked hands
note: Corn Huskers is mostly water and glycerin thickened with algin and guar. A home version is glycerin, aloe and water; without a preservative, keep it in the fridge and use within a week. The real bottle (about 5 dollars) is preserved and cheaper than most hand creams.

name: Lick-safe dog paw balm
claim: Protects paws from cold, salt and rough ground
note: For dogs. Melt, pour into a tin or push-up tube, and rub a thin layer on pads and the nose. No essential oils, no cocoa butter (dogs shouldn't lick it), and nothing scented. A little licked off is fine; see a vet for cracked, bleeding or swollen pads.

name: Safou and kpangnan whipped body butter
note: Based on the research notes' 15 to 30% safou and kpangnan phase whipped with shea. Melt the butters, add the oils, chill until just firm, then whip. Store cool; kpangnan softens in warm rooms.

name: Ximenia and marula face oil
note: A few drops over moisturizer. Both are stable oils; this softens and protects dry skin. It won't change blood flow or firm skin.

name: Mongongo hair shine oil
claim: Gloss and frizz control for lengths
note: A few drops on damp or dry ends. Mongongo is a light Kalahari oil traditionally used against dry desert air. Any protection from sun is minor; use a hat or a hair product with UV filters.

name: Atile resin skin balm
note: Warm the resin gently in the oil until it softens, strain, then melt in the beeswax and shea. Body only; resins can cause allergies, so patch test first.

name: Red onion and rosemary scalp spray (from the comments)
note: From a comment: blend and strain a red onion, add rosemary and a little oil, spray on the scalp once a week, cover 30 minutes, then wash. Simmer the rosemary in water first and cool it, then mix with the onion juice. Make a fresh batch each time and use it the same day. It can sting and smell strongly; the regrowth evidence is one small study in alopecia areata. Fuller-looking hair mostly comes from less breakage, as the creator herself says.

name: Postpartum herbal sitz bath
claim: Soothes a sore perineum after birth
note: Brew the herbs in hot water, strain very well through cheesecloth so no plant bits reach stitches, cool to lukewarm and add to a shallow sitz basin. Sit 10 to 15 minutes, then pat dry. Check with your midwife or doctor before soaking, and skip neem, moringa bark, rue and strong essential oils on torn or stitched skin. See a doctor for fever, foul discharge, or pain that's getting worse.

name: Okra detangling gel
claim: Melts tangles and makes wash day easier
note: Slice the okra, simmer in water for 10 to 15 minutes until slimy, cool and strain through a cloth. Apply to wet, sectioned hair, finger-detangle, then rinse. Make it fresh and use it within a day; okra gel spoils fast.

name: Pumpkin seed scalp oil
note: Massage a few drops into the scalp before wash day. It's a nice scalp oil; the hair-loss study used capsules taken by mouth, so don't expect the same from oil on the scalp. Iron, vitamin D and zinc matter only if you're low; ask a doctor for a blood test before supplementing.

name: Oil-free scalp tonic (Aromatica Tea Tree-style)
claim: Cooling care for an oily scalp that hates oils
note: For scalps that react to oils. Part your hair and dab onto the scalp, no rinsing. Tea tree stays well diluted. Without a preservative, keep it in the fridge and use within a week.

name: Light hair milk mist (leave-in alternative)
claim: Moisture for fine or low-density hair without weight
note: Like the Korean hair mists people use when leave-ins feel too heavy. Mist damp lengths and comb through. Panthenol and glycerin hold water in the hair. Fridge, use within a week.

name: Ambunu detangling wash (Chadian)
claim: Slippery herbal rinse that detangles and curl-defines
note: Steep in just-boiled water for 20 minutes, strain through a fine cloth, and let it cool. Pour over wet hair in sections, finger-detangle, then rinse. It cleans lightly; very oily scalps may still need shampoo.

name: Amla strengthening hair mask
note: Mix into a smooth paste, apply to damp lengths, leave 20 to 30 minutes, then rinse well and condition. Amla is mildly acidic: keep it off a scratched scalp. It can deepen color slightly on light or gray hair.

name: Bhringraj and brahmi hair oil
claim: Ayurvedic oil for scalp care and stronger-feeling hair
note: Warm the oils and powders in a double boiler on low for 1 hour, cool, then strain through a fine cloth. Massage a teaspoon into the scalp 1 to 2 hours before washing. Growth claims come from animal studies; it mostly conditions.

name: Whipped shea hair butter
note: Melt the shea gently, stir in the oils, chill 20 minutes until half-set, then whip until fluffy. Use a pea-sized amount on damp ends after a leave-in. Lots of it on fine or low-porosity hair can weigh it down.

name: Rosemary scalp tonic (tea, not oil)
claim: Refreshing daily scalp tonic like Korean root enhancers
note: Steep dried rosemary in just-boiled water for 15 minutes, strain, cool, then add glycerin. Spritz onto the scalp, massage, no rinsing. Use within 5 days. Rosemary isn't a proven hair-loss treatment; minoxidil is.

name: Light hair essence (non-greasy)
claim: Softness and shine without heavy oils
note: A DIY take on Korean hair essences and perfumed hair oils. Rub 2 to 3 drops between your palms and smooth over damp or dry ends. Skip the scent drops if your scalp is sensitive.

name: Coffee, besan and yogurt mask (face and body)
note: The popular "brown girl" coffee mask, with amounts filled in. Mix into a paste, smooth on (don't scrub), leave 10 minutes, rinse with lukewarm water. Use finely ground coffee. Turmeric can tint skin and towels yellow for a day. It leaves skin soft and looking fresher; it won't lighten underarms or fade dark spots.

name: Vanilla bean tincture (Sabahan-style)
claim: A natural vanilla base for perfume
note: Chop or pulse whole vanilla beans (pod and seeds) in a grinder you only use for perfume. Cover with perfumer's alcohol in a glass jar, about 10 g beans per 100 ml. Shake daily and steep 4 to 8 weeks somewhere dark, then strain through a coffee filter. More surface area extracts faster. Use it as a base note, diluted into a perfume.

name: Eucalyptus leaf tincture
claim: Cool, woody note that brightens sweet perfumes
note: Crush dried eucalyptus leaves, cover with perfumer's alcohol in a glass jar, shake daily and steep 2 to 4 weeks, then strain. Spray on clothes or pulse points, away from the face. Not for babies or young children: eucalyptus vapors can affect their breathing.

name: Green tea and herb hair rinse
claim: Herbal rinse for shine and a fresher scalp
note: Brew the tea, add the herbs, steep 20 minutes, strain and cool. Pour over clean hair on wash day, massage the scalp, leave a few minutes, then rinse or follow with conditioner. Once a week is plenty. Hibiscus can be added for shine but may tint light or gray hair reddish. If an herb makes your scalp itch (fenugreek does for some), leave it out.

name: Horsetail moisture spray (between wash days)
claim: For hair that feels dry mid-week
note: Steep horsetail in just-boiled water for 15 minutes, strain, cool, then mix in the aloe and glycerin. Mist onto lengths and seal with a little oil or butter. Keep in the fridge and use within 5 days. The silica claims aren't proven; the water and glycerin do the moisturizing.

name: Flyaway finishing stick
claim: Smooths baby hairs and flyaways without crunch
note: A DIY take on Thai hair finishing sticks. Melt everything together, pour into a clean lip balm tube or small tin, and let it set. Swipe a clean spoolie or toothbrush over it and brush down flyaways. Beeswax builds up, so wash it out with shampoo.

name: Perfumed body wash (Madame Fin-style)
claim: Skin that smells like perfume after the shower
note: Add the glycerin and scent to an unscented liquid castile soap or shower gel and shake. Don't add water: that dilutes the preservative. Rinse-off scent fades within hours; layer with a matching body oil if you want it to last.

name: Argan and coconut pre-wash hair mask
claim: Softer hair and less breakage on wash day
note: Warm in your hands and work through dry lengths 30 minutes to overnight before shampoo. Coconut oil soaks into hair and cuts protein loss when washing. Skip the coconut if your hair goes stiff with it.

name: Besan, yogurt and honey face mask (safer coffee-mask swap)
claim: Soft, fresher-looking face without scratchy grounds
note: The face version of the coffee mask: coffee grounds are too scratchy for facial skin, and turmeric can stain and irritate. Smooth on, leave 10 minutes, rinse with lukewarm water. Once or twice a week.

name: Coffee body mask (body version)
note: Keep the coffee for the body. Spread on damp skin in the shower, leave 5 to 10 minutes, then rinse while massaging gently. Skip freshly shaved areas. A pinch of turmeric is traditional, but it can stain and irritate, so it's left out here. It softens and polishes; it doesn't lighten skin.

name: Glass skin body wash (Haps-style dupe)
claim: Soft, comfortable skin after the shower
note: Haps Glass Skin Wash costs about $46. Its niacinamide and arbutin rinse off in seconds, so this skips them: an unscented gentle wash plus glycerin gives the same soft finish. The glow comes from the moisturizer you put on after.

name: Niacinamide face cream
claim: Hydrates, supports the barrier, evens tone over time
note: A properly formulated cream with 4% niacinamide for even tone and barrier support. (The Haps face cream turned out to have no niacinamide; see the ceramide barrier cream for that dupe.) Heat the water phase (water, glycerin, panthenol) and oil phase (Olivem, shea, squalane) separately to 70°C, blend, cool below 40°C, then stir in niacinamide dissolved in a little of the water and the preservative. Use a scale.

name: Brightening body lotion (Haps-style dupe)
claim: Evens tone on elbows, knees and marks, with daily sunscreen
note: Close to the Haps Illuminating Body Lotion (about $55) with 4% niacinamide and 2% alpha arbutin. The salicylic, lactic and azelaic acids are left out: they need pH testing and are easier to buy (AmLactin or CeraVe SA). Make it like the face cream: two heated phases, then add the actives and preservative below 40°C.

name: Licorice glycerin soap (Tana-style)
claim: Gentle clear bar with calming licorice
note: Tana Brightening Soap is a clear glycerin soap with niacinamide, licorice and herb extracts, plus fragrance. This melt-and-pour version keeps the gentle base and licorice, fragrance-free. Like any soap, it cleans; it won't fade dark spots.

name: Ceramide barrier cream (Haps anti-aging cream dupe)
claim: Barrier repair and all-day moisture, fragrance-free
note: Built from the Haps face cream's real ingredient list: squalane, petrolatum, ceramides and glycerin do the work. Its 16 plant extracts and two dyes are left out, along with the fragrance. Heat the water phase (water, glycerin, panthenol) and oil phase (Olivem, squalane, petrolatum) to 70°C, blend, cool below 40°C, then add the ceramide complex and preservative. Peptides are easier to buy ready-made (The Ordinary Multi-Peptide + HA) and layer under it.

name: Mineral toothpaste (as posted)
note: From the Bamglam post. Half a teaspoon of peppermint essential oil is a lot for the mouth. It has no fluoride, so it cleans but can't strengthen enamel or prevent cavities the way fluoride toothpaste does.

name: Mineral toothpaste (safer)
note: Same base with 3 drops of peppermint instead of half a teaspoon. Scoop with a clean spoon, never a wet brush, so water doesn't get into the jar. Use it alongside a fluoride toothpaste, not instead of one. Keep xylitol away from dogs.

name: Teeth whitening powder
note: Dip a wet brush, brush gently 2 minutes, rinse. Use 1 to 2 times a week and keep your fluoride toothpaste for daily use. It removes surface stains from coffee and tea; it doesn't bleach. Skip it with sensitive teeth, bleeding gums or worn enamel.

name: Eucalyptus mint decongesting soap
note: Melt and pour goat milk base, makes 8 to 10 bars. A spritz of rubbing alcohol on the surface pops bubbles; it evaporates before use, so it isn't counted. The menthol makes it tingle: keep it off the face and away from young children. The vapor feels freeing; it doesn't treat congestion.

name: Vegan hand cream with bakuchiol
note: A well-built cream: emulsifier, cetyl (counted as cetearyl) alcohol for body, and Geogard at about 0.8%. Heat water and oil phases separately to 70°C, blend, cool below 40°C, then add bakuchiol, vitamin E and preservative. Check the pH is 5 to 5.5 with strips.

name: Goat milk body gel lotion (as posted)
note: From the Lilyflower post, no amounts given; typical ones are filled in. Milk, aloe and oils stirred together without an emulsifier separate, and without a preservative the milk spoils within days in a pump bottle.

name: Goat milk body lotion (safer)
note: Uses goat milk powder (counted as powdered milk) dissolved into the water phase, an emulsifier and a broad-spectrum preservative. Heat phases to 70°C, blend, cool below 40°C, then add vitamin E, lavender and preservative. Skip the lavender for babies.

name: Bride-to-be glow mask
claim: Softer, brighter-looking skin before the big day
note: Ubtan-style mask; amounts filled in. Use pasteurized milk, not raw. Wild turmeric (kasturi) stains far less than kitchen turmeric. Coffee is kept to a fine pinch for the face. Patch test 2 weeks before the wedding, not the night before.

name: Fresh aloe and almond moisturizer (as posted)
note: The post says keep it 1 to 2 weeks in a cool, dry place. Fresh aloe gel is mostly water and spoils within days at room temperature.

name: Fresh aloe and almond moisturizer (safer)
claim: Soothing, made one use at a time
note: Mix one use in your palm and apply right away; keep the rest of the cut leaf wrapped in the fridge for up to a week. Rinse the cut leaf and let the yellow sap drain off first; it irritates. Skip the tea tree add-in on the face.

name: Breast milk soap (as posted)
claim: Gentle bar for baby and family
note: 200 g base with 5 oz (150 ml) breast milk makes a bar that's almost half milk. It stays soft, spoils, and needs the fridge or freezer, as the post says.

name: Breast milk bath (safer)
claim: Soothing bath for baby's dry skin
note: The safest way to use breast milk on skin: pour it into a warm baby bath and soak 5 to 10 minutes, then pat dry. No storing, no essential oils. If you make the soap instead, use only about 2 tablespoons of milk per 200 g of base, keep bars in the fridge and freeze extras.

name: Breast milk lotion (as posted)
note: 150 ml milk whisked into beeswax and oils, with no emulsifier or preservative. It separates and can grow bacteria within days.

name: Breast milk bum cream (as posted)
note: Milk in coconut oil and beeswax, unpreserved, used on broken diaper-area skin. Leave this one out. For diaper rash, a store zinc oxide or petrolatum cream works and is safe.

name: Milk-free baby bum balm
note: The safe version of the bum cream: no milk, no water, so it keeps. Melt shea and beeswax, stir in sunflower, then stir in zinc oxide (wear a mask while handling the powder). Fragrance-free. See a doctor for rash that blisters, bleeds or lasts more than 3 days.

name: Oat milk and shea bath bomb
note: Makes about 300 g. Spritz alcohol-free witch hazel a little at a time until the mix holds when squeezed; it evaporates as the bombs dry, so it isn't counted. Pack firmly, unmold, and dry 24 to 48 hours. Rinse the tub after: mica and petals can make it slippery.

name: Raw honey and milk facial cleanser
note: Mix fresh each time, massage 1 to 2 minutes, rinse with lukewarm water. Plant milks work too. It cleans lightly; it won't treat acne despite honey's antibacterial reputation.

name: Turkish rose scrub (Gül peelingi)
note: A single-use amount: the rose water means it can't be stored, so mix it just before your shower and use it all. For a jar that keeps, leave out the rose water. Body only, 1 to 2 times a week; sugar is too coarse for the face.

name: Ocean body soap (melt and pour)
note: A beginner version of the cold-process Ocean Detox Soap, with no lye to handle. Mix the powders into a spoonful of melted base first to avoid clumps. For the cold-process version, use the Soap tab Ocean bar preset; lye needs gloves, goggles and a 4 to 6 week cure.

name: Orange glow face mask (as posted)
note: A whole ground lemon on the face.

name: Orange glow face mask (safer)
note: Dried orange peel powder with yogurt and besan, no lemon. Leave 10 minutes, rinse, moisturize. Do it in the evening.

name: Whipped jojoba body butter
note: The post calls this a lotion, but with no water it's a body butter. Melt shea, coconut and beeswax, cool slightly, add jojoba and essential oil, then whip as it sets. It's heavy for oily faces despite the post: coconut oil clogs pores for many people, so keep it to the body.

name: Vanilla perfumed body powder (talc-free)
claim: Soft scent and a silky dry finish
note: A DIY take on perfumed powders like Sherry Venus. Sift the arrowroot and mica, add the scent drop by drop while whisking, then let it sit 2 days in a closed jar. Pat on with a puff away from your face to avoid breathing it in. Not for babies.

name: Coconut rice milk shower polish
claim: Creamy scrub that cleans and smooths
note: From TheGlowUpGear. Mostly preserved shower gel, so it keeps better than an oil scrub, but scoop with a dry hand and keep shower water out. Use within a month rather than the 3 months the post says, since the rice and milk powders dilute the gel's preservative.

name: Brown sugar scrub (Brooklyn Botany dupe)
note: A copy of the store scrub's three main ingredients. Brown sugar is softer than white, but still body only, not face. 1 to 2 times a week, never on freshly shaved skin.

name: Aloe vera leave-in detangler (preserved)
note: Same spray with 1% Geogard ECT so it keeps 2 to 3 months. Shake before each use; the oil floats.

name: Shea hair butter (Crystal DIY)
note: Melt the coconut, stir everything together, chill 20 to 30 minutes until slightly firm, then whip. Skip the lavender on sensitive scalps.

name: Hand oil (sold as anti-aging)
note: A nice nail and cuticle oil. The before and after photo isn't real: oils soften and moisturize, but they don't remove wrinkles or sun spots. For those, use daily sunscreen on your hands and a retinoid or vitamin C cream.

name: Coffee glow body scrub
note: Use 1 to 2 times a week. Coffee scrubs stain grout and clog drains; rinse the shower after. Glow here means smoother skin, not lighter.

name: Lemon sugar polish
note: Fine as a rinse-off scrub. Cold-pressed lemon oil can make skin react to sun, so use it in the evening, or swap in steam-distilled lemon oil, which doesn't. It won't brighten beyond the smoothness of any scrub.

name: Simple coffee body scrub with body wash
note: Mix one use at a time; the body wash adds water. It won't remove a tan or improve circulation, but it smooths.

name: Coffee vanilla body scrub (sold for cellulite)
note: Cellulite is how fat sits under the skin's connective bands; no scrub removes it. Massage and caffeine can make skin look smoother for a few hours. Cinnamon powder can irritate; patch test.

name: Glow boost turmeric body scrub
note: 2 tablespoons of turmeric will stain skin, towels and grout yellow. Use 1 teaspoon, or wild turmeric (kasturi), which stains far less.

name: Epsom salt and sweet almond oil scrub
note: Salt stings cuts and freshly shaved skin. Body only. It won't absorb magnesium through the skin in any meaningful way, but it feels lovely.

name: Aloe turmeric night cream (as posted)
note: Fresh aloe stored 2 weeks with no preservative grows bacteria, and a full teaspoon of turmeric in 2 tbsp stains skin and pillowcases yellow.

name: Aloe and rose water night gel (safer)
note: Use store-bought pure aloe gel (it's preserved) and pat rose water on first instead of mixing it in, and skip the turmeric overnight. Keep in the fridge and use within 2 weeks. For glow, add a few drops of glycerin.

name: Butterfly pea "collagen" gel
note: Well built: preserved, pH 5 to 5.5 checked, 100 g batch. Marine collagen in a gel works as a humectant; it can't rebuild your collagen. Butterfly pea gives the color. Fish allergy? Skip the collagen.

name: Brightening deodorant cream (BamGlamDIY)
note: A good baking-soda-free formula: zinc ricinoleate and zinc oxide handle odor, arrowroot and kaolin absorb. It won't lighten underarms; less shaving friction helps more. The preservative isn't needed with no water, but doesn't hurt.

name: Lavender relaxing balm
note: Rub on wrists, neck and feet, away from eyes. Lavender's scent can help you unwind; it isn't a sleep treatment.

name: Rosemary castile shampoo (as posted)
note: Rosemary tea and aloe in a shampoo bottle with no preservative spoils within a week. Castile soap is alkaline; follow with an acidic rinse or conditioner or hair can feel rough.

name: Rosemary castile shampoo (safer)
note: No tea or aloe in the bottle: add a splash of rosemary tea to each wash instead, or mix a single wash in your palm. Follow with conditioner.

name: D-tan soap (melt and pour)
claim: Gentle cleanse with a nice scent
note: Based on the D-Tan soap list. Like any soap, it washes off; it won't remove a tan, which fades as skin renews. Coffee and rice flour add a soft scrub.

name: Charcoal and tea tree soap (melt and pour)
note: Charcoal makes lather look dramatic, but in a soap it rinses off before it can do much for acne or pores. A benzoyl peroxide or salicylic wash does more. Lovely for the body.

name: Coffee scrub (5-recipe card)
note: Mix one use. Coffee doesn't firm skin or improve circulation for more than a few minutes.

name: Sugar and honey scrub
note: Skip the optional lemon juice. Body only.

name: Lemon and sea salt scrub (as posted)
note: Lemon juice on freshly scrubbed skin can burn in sunlight, and salt stings any nicks.

name: Sea salt and olive scrub (safer)
note: Lemon juice swapped for a few drops of steam-distilled lemon oil. Not on shaved skin.

name: Turmeric and yogurt scrub
note: 2 tablespoons of turmeric stains; 1/2 teaspoon is plenty. It won't fight acne. Rice flour gives the scrub.

name: Cloud soft body butter for kids
claim: Rich moisture for dry kids' skin
note: Well built for ages 1+, 300 g batch. Contains almond (tree nut). Leave the scent out for under-3s or eczema-prone skin; the chamomile or vanilla is optional.

name: Deep muscle relief body oil
note: About 0.7% essential oils, a sensible body dilution. Warming massage eases tension; it doesn't treat joint inflammation. Black pepper and ginger can tingle, so wash hands after and keep away from eyes.

name: Revive leg and foot oil
note: 1% essential oils. Massaging upward toward the heart feels good and can ease puffiness for a while; the oils themselves don't boost circulation. Swollen legs that don't settle overnight need a doctor.

name: Chest calm sleep blend
note: A gentle 1% blend with bergamot FCF, the version that doesn't cause sun reactions. It helps you unwind; it doesn't open airways. Not for children under 6 near the face.

name: Healing heel oil
note: Rub in at night and wear socks. Oils soften heels; for deep cracks, a urea 10 to 25% foot cream works faster. The before and after photo is optimistic for oil alone.

name: Almond powder and honey scrub
note: Mix a fresh spoonful each use (the post's half cup would sit in a jar). Finely ground almond is gentle enough for the face. Tree nut: skip with nut allergies.

name: Gram flour and turmeric scrub
note: Use pasteurized milk or yogurt rather than raw milk. Leave 5 to 10 minutes and rinse. It won't remove a tan or treat acne.

name: Coffee and coconut oil scrub
note: Body only; coffee grounds are too scratchy for the face, despite the photos. Coconut oil can clog facial pores too.

name: Rice flour and milk scrub
note: Mix fresh each time. Fine rice flour is a gentle face polish. It won't lighten skin.

name: Brown sugar and olive oil scrub
note: Body only, not face as shown: sugar crystals can scratch facial skin.

name: Coffee scrub with baby oil and lotion
note: Baby oil is mineral oil, a safe, gentle moisturizer. The lotion and body wash bring water into the jar, though, and the photo shows a whitening lotion. Mix one use at a time with plain lotion, or skip the lotion and wash.

name: Rose glow polish
note: From the body polishes card; amounts filled in. Body only.

name: Oatmeal soothing polish
note: Amounts filled in. A few drops of lavender at most, or none for sensitive skin.

name: Lemon detox polish
note: Amounts filled in. Dried lemon peel powder keeps in the jar where fresh zest would spoil; use it in the evening. It doesn't detox. Salt stings shaved skin.

name: Chamomile and jasmine foaming scrub
claim: Cleanse and exfoliate in one step
note: Inspired by Luna and Lavender; amounts filled in. A no-water foaming scrub: soap base melted and stirred with oils and sugar. Keep water out of the jar. The app flags the oil level because it would make a soft bar; that's intended here, since this stays a soft scrub.

name: Rice and saffron glow mask
note: Soak rice in milk 2 to 3 hours in the fridge, not on the counter, then blend with saffron. Leave 15 minutes and rinse. Saffron gives a golden tint; it won't reduce pigmentation.

name: Fennel powdered cleanser for oily skin
note: A dry powder keeps well; mix a teaspoon with water in your palm each time. Bentonite is drying, so once a day at most and moisturize after. It won't shrink pores.

name: Lavender and oat cleansing powder
note: Inspired by Luna and Lavender; amounts filled in. Coconut milk powder stands in for the coconut milk so the jar stays dry. Mix a teaspoon with water each use.

name: Coffee scrub for oily skin (as posted)
note: Coffee grounds are too scratchy for facial skin, especially on breakouts. Use it on the body instead.

name: Yogurt honey mask for oily skin (safer)
claim: Gentle cleanse for oily, breakout-prone skin
note: The coffee swapped for fine oat powder. Leave on 10 minutes and rinse. For real breakouts, a salicylic or benzoyl peroxide product does more.

name: Orange sugar foot scrub (as posted)
note: Fresh orange juice and zest in a stored jar of scrub spoil within days.

name: Orange sugar foot scrub (safer)
note: Juice and fresh zest swapped for dried orange peel powder so it keeps. Rinse the tub after; oily feet slip.

name: Gram flour and orange peel glow mask
note: Keep the dry mix in a jar and add water per use. Turmeric at 1/2 tsp can still tint skin; wild turmeric stains less.

name: Rice, besan and turmeric scrub powder
note: Mix 1 to 2 tsp with water or milk per use. It won't fade a tan or fight acne.

name: Pomegranate body wash
note: Mostly well built and preserved. 1/4 tsp Geogard is about 0.4%, the bottom of its range, so use 1/2 tsp. "Pomegranate extract" is counted as water.

name: Oat and honey castile shampoo (one wash)
claim: Gentle wash for a dry, itchy scalp
note: Mix one wash in a cup: castile soap, cooled oat water and honey, used straight away. Castile is alkaline, so follow with conditioner or a diluted vinegar rinse. Skip the coconut oil if your hair goes stiff with it.

name: Oatmeal castile shampoo (as posted)
note: Oat water, honey and aloe in a bottle with no preservative spoil within days.

name: Coconut milk castile shampoo (as posted)
note: A full cup of coconut milk in a shampoo bottle spoils within days, even in the fridge.

name: Neem soapnut wash (fresh)
claim: Gentle wash for a flaky scalp
note: Make one wash: boil the soapnuts, neem and fenugreek in 2 cups water for 20 minutes, cool, strain and use the same day. Fenugreek can trigger legume allergies. For real dandruff, ketoconazole or zinc pyrithione shampoo works better.

name: Neem and guava leaf scalp rinse
note: Boil a handful of each in 2 to 3 cups water for 10 to 15 minutes, cool, strain, and use the same day as a final rinse.

name: Curry leaf coconut hair oil
note: Dry the leaves completely before frying gently in the oil; any water makes the oil spoil and can spatter. Strain well. It conditions hair; growth and anti-graying claims aren't backed by studies.

name: Hibiscus reetha shikakai shampoo (as posted)
note: From cozyselfcarequeen. The post honestly says 7 to 10 days in the fridge, which is about right for an unpreserved herbal tea; the aloe makes it spoil faster.

name: Hibiscus reetha wash (one wash)
note: Halve the batch, skip the aloe, and use it the same day. Shikakai and reetha clean gently; keep it out of the eyes, it stings. The growth claims aren't proven.

name: Rosemary mint shampoo bar (melt and pour)
note: A well-built 500 g batch. 5 g peppermint oil (about 100 drops) is 1%, which tingles noticeably; drop to 2 to 3 g for sensitive scalps. Rosemary powder refreshes; it isn't a proven hair-loss treatment.

name: Beetroot scrub (as posted)
note: Fresh grated beet, honey and rose water spoil quickly even in the fridge, and brown sugar is too sharp for the face.

name: Beetroot sugar body scrub (safer)
note: Beetroot powder instead of fresh beet so it keeps; body only. It tints skin and towels pink briefly. It won't fade dark spots.

name: Gold glow gel (as posted)
note: Fresh aloe stored 7 to 10 days unpreserved can grow bacteria. Gold adds sparkle only; it doesn't brighten, firm or fade spots.

name: Gold shimmer aloe gel (safer)
note: Store-bought pure aloe gel (already preserved) instead of fresh, so it keeps 1 to 2 months in the fridge. Avoid the eye area: glitter flakes irritate eyes.

name: Hair primer spray (Crystal DIY)
note: Well thought out and preserved. The post's teaspoon of conditioner is swapped here for polysorbate 20, which mixes the oils into the water more reliably. Shake before each use. Heat protection from this is mild; a silicone heat protectant does more for flat irons.

name: Rosemary water hair spray (as posted)
note: Rosemary tea keeps about a week in the fridge, as the post says. Spritz on the scalp; it's refreshing, but the growth study used rosemary oil, and even that was small.

name: Sage leaf scalp oil
note: Infuse dried sage in grapeseed oil for 3 weeks, shaking daily, then strain. Massage 1 tsp into the scalp, leave 20 minutes, then shampoo. Oil doesn't reduce scalp oil; shampooing afterward does the cleaning.

name: Rosemary scalp oil (infused)
note: Use dried rosemary, or dry fresh sprigs completely first; water in oil grows mold. Warm on low 10 to 15 minutes, cool, strain.

name: Citrus milk bath
note: Use steam-distilled lemon oil, or skip the lemon oil and zest if you'll be in the sun after. Mix the essential oils into the milk powder first so they don't float on the water. Dried peel stands in for fresh zest, and the drops are halved to a sensible amount for one bath.

name: Rose pink milk bath
note: Amounts filled in; makes 4 baths. Beet powder tints the water pink, not the skin. Rinse the tub after so petals don't clog the drain.

name: Mineral bath soak
note: Amounts filled in. Salts feel soothing; skin absorbs little magnesium, and baths don't draw out toxins or support organs. Pink salt's trace minerals are tiny amounts.

name: Calendula and lavender bath tea
note: Like the Chambers Botanical bags. Fill tea bags or muslin with 2 tbsp each, steep in the bath 10 minutes.

name: Powdered milk bath (Creative Homemaking)
note: Makes about 2 1/4 cups; use 1/2 to 1 cup per bath. Mix the essential oil into the powders well so it doesn't float. Rinse the tub after; petals and milk leave a film.

name: Chamomile relaxing foot soak
claim: Calm, soft feet after a long day
note: Sold as an "adrenal support" soak. It's a lovely wind-down; it doesn't change hormones or adrenal function. Keep the water warm, not hot, especially with diabetes or poor feeling in the feet.

name: Stimulating herbal bath tea (LisaBee-style)
note: Amounts filled in for 2 bags. Dried orange slices and lemon peel stay fine when fully dried. Rinse the tub so salts and peel don't stain.

name: Undereye care cream (as posted)
note: Aloe, rose water and hyaluronic solution beaten into oils and beeswax with no emulsifier separate, and with no preservative they grow mold near your eyes. Caffeine and niacinamide at 0.5 g are reasonable amounts.

name: Caffeine eye gel (safer undereye)
claim: Less puffy-looking eyes in the morning
note: The water-based actives without the oils, in a preserved gel, about 1% caffeine and 2% niacinamide. Dissolve caffeine and niacinamide in warm water, stir into the aloe, add the preservative. Pat a tiny amount on the orbital bone, not the lid. Dark circles from genetics or shadows won't fade.

name: Overnight eye butter
note: Water-free, so the Leucidal isn't needed. Leave out the frankincense and chamomile oils near the eyes; one drop each in this tiny batch is still a lot. Sea buckthorn is cut from 1/2 tsp to 2 drops; more tints skin orange. Fine lines plump temporarily; dark circles stay.

name: Creamy cleansing balm (Tessa's)
note: Makes about 4 oz. Fractionated coconut is counted as MCT oil. Without an emulsifier it doesn't rinse milky; wipe off with a warm cloth. Skip the essential oils if you'll use it around your eyes.

name: Shimmer eyeshadow (Tessa's)
note: Use cosmetic-grade, eye-safe micas only (some reds and craft micas aren't approved near eyes). Silk powder or boron nitride is counted as arrowroot. Wear a mask while mixing powders. Clean brushes often.

name: Lip oil gloss (BamGlamDIY)
note: 30 g batch from the percentages. Versagel is mineral oil gelled with polymers, counted here as mineral oil; it's safe on lips. Use lip-safe micas only.

name: Balanced lip oil (non-sticky)
note: 30 g batch from the percentages. A well-balanced, water-free formula. Use a lip-safe flavor oil at 0.5%.

name: Chamomile powdered cleanser (dry mix)
note: The post's own "or" option: keep the dry powders in a jar and mix a teaspoon with plant milk and a drop of honey at the sink. The blended wet version only lasts days in the fridge.

name: Frankincense and myrrh bath bomb
note: Makes 3 to 4 bombs, so each holds about 5 drops of oil (the checker counts the whole batch as one bath). Spritz the witch hazel in slowly; it evaporates as they dry. Mix the oils into the almond oil first. Rinse the tub; petals clog drains.

name: Green tea soak (detox-style)
note: 500 g batch; use 50 to 100 g per bath. 5 g fragrance oil in 500 g is about 1%, fine in a bath. Loose green tea leaves are counted as green tea powder; put them in a muslin bag so they don't clog the drain. Baths don't detox or tighten skin.

name: Citrus energy shower melts
claim: Uplifting citrus steam in the morning shower
note: Place on the shower floor away from the stream. Cold-pressed citrus oils are fine here since they don't stay on skin. Breathe the steam; it lifts your mood but doesn't clean the air. Keep away from children and pets.

name: Chamomile cleanser for dry or mature skin (as posted)
note: Makes 1.5 litres of herbal tea with honey and aloe and no preservative. The post honestly says to discard after a week, but that's far more than anyone uses in a week, and it may spoil sooner. Alfalfa and fennel are counted in the herbal tea.

name: Chamomile milky cleanser (small batch)
note: A tenth of the batch: steep 3 g each of chamomile and calendula in 150 ml just-boiled water, strain, then stir in glycerin and honey. Fridge, use within 5 days. It cleans lightly, like a rinse; it won't remove makeup or sunscreen.

name: Floral rose perfume (100 ml spray, as posted)
note: About 15% scent in perfumer's alcohol, eau de parfum strength. Best sprayed on clothes and hair rather than skin, where that much ylang and rose can sensitize over time; the 5 ml water is fine in this much alcohol. Real rose oil is costly; rose fragrance oil works. Spray on clothes or pulse points away from the face, patch test first, and keep it from sunlit skin if you swap in citrus.

name: Floral rose perfume oil (roll-on, safer)
claim: A soft rose scent for pulse points
note: A roll-on version at a skin-friendly strength: 10 ml jojoba with 6 drops of the same blend. The 100 ml spray from the post is about 15% scent; that works on clothes and hair, not repeated on skin. Ylang ylang is kept low because it's a common allergen.

name: Scalp detox scrub with jojoba and tea tree
note: Mix one use. Once every 1 to 2 weeks, fingertips only; sugar can scratch, so skip it on a sore or broken scalp. Shampoo after. It doesn't detox; it lifts buildup and flakes.

name: Acne-calming serum (as posted)
note: Aloe and vitamin C powder in jojoba with no emulsifier or preservative separates and can grow mold within days, not the 2 to 3 weeks the post says. Vitamin C powder doesn't treat acne.

name: Brightening vitamin C serum (as posted)
note: Vitamin C dissolved in rose water oxidizes (turns yellow-brown) within days, and the oil floats on top. An unpreserved water serum shouldn't be kept 7 to 10 days.

name: Fresh vitamin C mix (one use)
note: The safer way to use vitamin C powder: a pinch dissolved in a few drops of water in your palm, used right away at night. It tingles; stop if it stings. A stable store serum (or vitamin C derivative) works better for dark spots.

name: Hydrating glow serum (as posted)
note: Fresh cucumber juice in a stored serum spoils within a day or two, as the post itself warns.

name: Glycerin aloe hydrating serum (safer)
note: No cucumber juice. Store-bought aloe already has a preservative; adding 1% Geogard covers the extra water. Use 2 to 3 drops on damp skin, then moisturizer.

name: Basil and cucumber face toner (as posted)
note: Fresh cucumber and basil juice in a spray bottle spoils within a day or two, and undiluted tea tree drops don't mix into water; they float and can irritate.

name: Cucumber cooling compress (fresh)
note: Blend a few slices of cucumber with a little rose water, strain, and pat on with cotton the same day. No tea tree. Throw away any leftover.

name: Glow up skin serum (as posted)
note: About 80 drops of essential oils in a 2 oz bottle is around 7%, far above the 1% safe for the face. Copaiba and yarrow aren't counted.

name: Glow up face oil (safer)
note: The same four oils with the scent cut to 12 drops (about 1%). Press 3 to 4 drops into damp skin at night. Argan and almond are nuts.

name: Nightly glow serum (as posted)
note: 25 drops of essential oil topped up with jojoba in a typical 30 ml dropper is about 4%, too strong for nightly face use.

name: Nightly glow serum (safer)
note: Cut to 4 drops in 30 ml jojoba (well under 1%), gentle enough for nightly use.

name: Homemade zinc sunscreen (as posted)
note: Zinc stirred into oils and wax doesn't spread evenly and has never been SPF-tested; you can't know if it protects at SPF 2 or 20. Use a tested mineral sunscreen.

name: Scars vanishing night mask (as posted)
note: Licorice powder, aloe and vitamin C left on overnight and stored with no preservative. A "cure time" of 21 days means it sits and spoils. No mask makes scars vanish; vitamin C serum mixed into powder breaks down fast.

name: Licorice and aloe calming mask (fresh)
note: Mix one use, leave 10 to 15 minutes, rinse. Licorice gently calms redness. For marks and old scars, azelaic acid, niacinamide and sunscreen do more; deep scars need a dermatologist.

name: Overnight face barrier repair balm (BamGlamDIY)
note: Well built and water-free, so it keeps 9 to 12 months. Aloe-infused oil is counted as almond oil. Petrolatum doesn't clog pores in studies, but this is heavy: best for dry, irritated or winter skin, as the last step at night.

name: Green clay poultice mask
note: Mix 1 tbsp clay with water to a paste; add 1 drop tea tree at most. Rinse before it dries fully (about 10 minutes). It absorbs oil; it doesn't detox.

name: Green clay shoulder compress
claim: A cooling compress for sore muscles
note: The cold clay feels soothing for 20 to 30 minutes, then rinse. It doesn't draw out pain or inflammation; for injury, rest and ice or a doctor. Amounts filled in.

name: Sidr, milk and honey softening mask
note: Thin layer, 5 to 10 minutes, rinse before it dries, then moisturize. Sidr can be drying, as the card honestly says. Patch test first.

name: Matcha glow mask
note: Amounts filled in. Matcha's antioxidants are nice in a rinse-off mask, but it won't clear acne or dark spots. Rice flour gives a gentle polish.

name: Kaolin and green tea pore mask
note: T-zone only, 5 to 8 minutes, rinse before it dries, 1 to 2 times a week. It absorbs oil; pores can't be shrunk or "refined" permanently.

name: Gentle kaolin mask for dry, sensitive skin
claim: A mild cleanse that doesn't strip
note: 8 to 10 minutes, don't let it dry fully, then moisturize. Kaolin is the gentlest clay; bentonite and multani mitti are more drying.

name: Vanilla honey lip balm
note: Honey and watery vanilla extract don't mix into the wax; they sink and bead. Stir constantly as it cools, or swap for a lip-safe vanilla flavor oil. A lot of wax makes it firm, which suits tubes.

name: Strawberry shea lip balm
claim: Soft, tinted lips with a fruity scent
note: Use a lip-safe strawberry flavor oil, not a watery baking extract; 8 drops is plenty (the post's 1/2 tsp is too strong). A tiny pinch of beetroot powder tints pink; more gets gritty.

name: Rose shea lip balm (Crystal DIY)
note: Simple and well balanced. Rose essential oil at 3 drops is fine; rose fragrance oil works if it's lip-safe.

name: Under-eye night cream (aloe and almond)
note: Aloe and almond oil stirred together separate without an emulsifier, and 7 to 10 days in the fridge without a preservative is optimistic near the eyes. It won't fade dark circles.

name: Honey, rose and oat face cleanser
note: Honey with no water keeps a few weeks if you scoop with a dry spoon. Grind the oats fine for the face. Rinse with warm water.

name: Pomegranate scrub (as posted)
note: Fresh pomegranate seeds and rose water in a stored jar spoil within days. It won't unclog pores or even skin tone.

name: Pomegranate scrub (fresh, one use)
note: Make it in the shower and use it all. Crush a spoonful of seeds into the sugar and oil. Body only.

name: Evening rose and chamomile tonic
claim: Calming toner for dry, sensitive skin
note: Fridge, use within 5 to 7 days as the card says. Chamomile is in the daisy family; skip with ragweed allergy.

name: Coconut and vanilla body polish
claim: Soft skin with a sweet scent
note: Keep the jar dry; vanilla extract is mostly alcohol and water, so vanilla powder keeps better. Body only.

name: Lavender castile facial cleanser (as posted)
note: Castile soap is alkaline (pH 9 to 10), which can leave facial skin tight; it's better on the body. With water and honey added it needs the fridge and a week at most, as the card says.

name: Dandelion and thyme vinegar toner
note: The vinegar keeps it months. Dilute 1 part infused vinegar to at least 4 parts water; neat vinegar burns. Thyme isn't a proven acne treatment. The checker flags vinegar left on skin; if you use it, dab it on oily areas only and rinse after a minute or two. Don't drink it as a "tonic" without asking a doctor, especially in pregnancy.

name: Oat water skin soak
note: Make fresh each time: soak 2 tbsp oats in 1 cup water 10 to 15 minutes, strain, and lay a soaked cloth on skin. Lovely for eczema-prone skin; colloidal oatmeal is a real skin protectant.

name: Honey and oat cream cleanser
note: Castile soap's high pH helps it resist spoilage, so this keeps a few weeks if no water gets in. Shake before use; the oatmeal settles. Castile is alkaline, so it can leave dry facial skin tight: try it on the body first, or follow with moisturizer.

name: Almond powder mask for dry skin
note: Amounts filled in. Blanch and grind almonds fine, or buy almond flour. 10 to 15 minutes, rinse with gentle circles. Tree nut.

name: Almond powder mask for oily skin
claim: A gentle polish for oily skin
note: Amounts filled in. Matcha adds antioxidants; it won't clear acne. Tree nut.

name: Turmeric and milk face mask
note: 10 to 15 minutes, rinse well. Turmeric stains; it won't treat acne or dark spots.

name: Glowy hydrating body mist (as posted)
note: A cup of water with aloe and glycerin and no preservative spoils within a week. Mica settles; shake well.

name: Glowy shimmer body mist (preserved)
claim: Dewy glow with a soft shimmer
note: The same mist with 1% Geogard so it keeps 2 to 3 months. Shake before every spray. Avoid the face and eyes.

name: Natural shaving cream (as posted)
note: Aloe whipped into coconut and shea without an emulsifier separates and grows mold in the shower. It won't prevent razor bumps.

name: Whipped shave butter (no water)
note: Water-free, so it keeps. Apply a thin layer to wet skin; it rinses clean. Oil can clog razors; rinse the blade often.

name: Gold luxury spa body oil
note: Well balanced at about 0.8% essential oils. Shake before use; mica settles. Cosmetic-grade mica only. Argan is a tree nut.

name: Mint and lavender body polish
note: A thoughtful recipe: fine sugar, jojoba, and a pre-diluted fragrance instead of neat essential oils. Once a week; skip shaved or irritated skin.

name: Cucumber gel for summer (as posted)
note: Fresh cucumber juice spoils within a day or two, not 7 to 10, and tea tree drops float in water.

name: Lip serum with honey (as posted)
note: Honey doesn't dissolve in oil; it sinks to the bottom of a roller bottle.

name: Herbal rose lavender lip oil
note: Dried petals infused 1 to 2 weeks then strained, so no water. Use lavender at 3 drops only.

name: Rose lip butter with dragon fruit
note: Amounts filled in. Freeze-dried dragon fruit powder tints pink; a pinch only. Strain rose-infused oil well.

name: Soft pink lip balm (honey)
note: Honey beads in the wax; stir as it cools.

name: Plumping lip gloss (Tessa's)
note: Peppermint and cinnamon irritate lips to make them swell slightly; it lasts minutes. Cinnamon bark is a strong allergen even at half a drop. Germall isn't needed in a water-free oil.

name: Simple lip oil (BamGlamDIY)
note: 30 g batch: well balanced and water-free.

name: Bridal glow body oil
note: Well built, 100 g. The optional fragrance (17 drops) is under 1%. Mica only cosmetic grade.

name: Lip sleeping mask (BamGlam Spa)
note: 100 g, water-free and well balanced. Lanolin is a top-tier lip sealant; patch test if you have eczema or wool allergy.

name: Khumra-inspired perfume oil (safer)
note: Inspired by Sudanese khumra, at a skin-safe strength. Warm 1 tsp mahlab in the sesame oil on low for 20 minutes, cool, strain well, then add the essential oils. Clove is kept to 1 drop because it's a strong skin sensitizer. Dab on wrists and behind the ears; patch test first. Traditional khumra is far more concentrated and often contains synthetic musks, so wear it on hair, scarves and clothes rather than broken or sensitive skin.

name: Frankincense, rose and olive body oil
claim: Soft, scented skin after the shower
note: 100 ml at about 1.5% essential oil, a sensible full-body strength. Press into damp skin after a shower. Frankincense oil oxidizes and becomes more irritating with age, so buy fresh and keep the bottle dark and cool; it keeps 6 to 12 months. Extra virgin olive oil is rich and smells of olives; swap in half jojoba or sunflower for a lighter feel. It softens skin but doesn't tone or tighten it.

name: Frankincense and rose infused olive oil (whole plant)
claim: A gently scented body oil from resin and petals
note: Warm dried rose petals and crushed frankincense tears in the oil over a double boiler, below 50°C, for 2 to 3 hours, then strain through fine cloth. Petals must be bone dry. Resin only partly dissolves in oil, so the scent is soft. No essential oils, so it suits sensitive skin better than the essential oil version.

name: Foaming apricot, saffron and glycolic scrub (as posted)
note: Sharp apricot shell plus glycolic acid is double exfoliation; together they can leave skin raw, especially on shaved or darker skin prone to marks. Saffron adds colour, not results.

name: Foaming sugar and saffron scrub (safer)
claim: Smooth skin with a soft lather
note: No-water foaming scrub: stir sugar and oil into shower gel, keep water out of the jar. Use 1 to 2 times a week. If you want glycolic, use it as a leave-on lotion on other nights, not in the scrub.

name: Ewedu (jute leaf) slippery hair wash
claim: Detangles and gently cleanses curly hair
note: Soak or blend a handful of fresh leaves in warm water until slimy, strain through cloth, pour over wet hair, finger-detangle and rinse. Make it fresh each time. Check it really is jute leaf, not Sida acuta.

name: Japanese rice milk soap (melt and pour)
note: Inspired by Dreaminfinite's rice milk bar. Rice flour and milk powder go into a little melted base first, then the rest. Hinoki gives a calm Japanese cypress scent. Like any soap it cleans; moisturize after.

name: Sensitive skin bar (fragrance-free chamomile)
note: Like Apo.Ge's sensitive bar: no scent at all. Steep chamomile in a spoon of hot water, strain, and stir the cooled tea and oats into melted base. Skip with ragweed allergy.

name: Clear bar (turmeric and kaolin)
claim: For oily skin and body breakouts
note: Like Apo.Ge's clear bar. A pinch of turmeric tints; more stains. Soap rinses off, so it won't treat acne; a benzoyl peroxide wash does more for body breakouts.

name: Balance bar (green clay and tea tree)
note: Like Apo.Ge's balance bar, for oily skin or grimy hands.

name: Plant jelly balm (Vaseline alternative)
claim: Seals in moisture like petroleum jelly
note: A DIY nod to plant jellies like Cerabellina (a castor-based wax jelly). Melt beeswax into castor and sunflower, stir as it cools for a soft jelly. Thin layer on dry hands, lips, heels. Petroleum jelly still seals better and is very safe.

name: Turmeric, honey and milk powder face mask
note: From a comment that also adds lemon; lemon is left out (it burns in sunlight). 10 minutes, rinse well. Turmeric stains.

name: Spiced shampoo booster (rosemary, clove, cinnamon, ginger)
note: Stirring ground spices into shampoo makes it gritty, and cinnamon and clove are strong skin irritants on the scalp. Brew a rosemary and ginger tea for a separate rinse instead.

name: Rosemary and ginger scalp rinse (safer spice swap)
note: Steep 1 tbsp dried rosemary and a few slices of ginger in 2 cups just-boiled water for 15 minutes, strain, cool, pour over the scalp after shampoo. Make it fresh.

name: Tamarind coffee body scrub (Skin Editor dupe)
note: Copies the tamarind and coffee scrub idea. Tamarind's natural acids give a gentle extra polish. Fresh pulp, so mix one use and rinse well. The niacinamide and black pearl in the store version mostly rinse off.

name: Guava hand cream (Trader Joe's dupe)
note: A preserved cream in the spirit of the guava hand cream. Heat water and oil phases to 70°C, blend, cool below 40°C, add vitamin E, fragrance and preservative. Guava scent comes from a skin-safe fragrance oil; guava leaf adds nothing proven.

name: Fig, black tea and musk perfume oil
note: Inspired by the after-the-rain layering trend. A skin-safe fig fragrance oil and white musk in jojoba; steep a teaspoon of black tea leaves in the jojoba for a week and strain for the tea note. Patch test.

name: Ultra moisturizing hand cream (Trader Joe's original dupe)
note: Mirrors the original's oils: 20% shea plus coconut, hemp, sunflower and almond, preserved. Heat the water phase (water, glycerin) and oil phase (shea, oils, emulsifier) to 70°C, blend, cool below 40°C, add vitamin E and preservative. Fragrance-free; the comment that the original "doesn't agree" with someone may be the hemp, so swap it for more sunflower if needed. Contains almond.

name: Pumpkin spice hand cream (gentler TJ-style)
note: The store pumpkin cream lists coumarin, cinnamal and eugenol, spice-scent allergens. This version is the hand cream base with a little pumpkin seed oil and a skin-safe pumpkin spice fragrance oil at 0.5% instead of real cinnamon or clove oil.

name: Unscented deodorant stick (Trader Joe's dupe)
claim: Odor control without baking soda or aluminum
note: Same idea as the TJ stick: arrowroot and zinc ricinoleate absorb and neutralize odor, coconut and jojoba keep it smooth. Melt shea, coconut and beeswax, stir in the powders, pour into a tube. It's a deodorant, so you'll still sweat.

name: Leave-in conditioner spray (Trader Joe's dupe)
note: Inspired by the TJ leave-in's argan, vitamin E and evening primrose. Polysorbate keeps the oils mixed; panthenol stands in for pea protein (add 1% hydrolyzed plant protein if you have it). Preserved, so it keeps 2 to 3 months. Mist on damp lengths, avoid roots. It won't make 450°F safe for hair.

name: Shine hair serum (Trader Joe's dupe, water-free)
note: The TJ serum is a creamy leave-in with coconut, shea, argan, vitamin E and panthenol. This water-free oil version keeps without a preservative: melt the shea into the oils, shake before use, and use a pea-sized amount on mid-lengths and ends.

name: Coconut body butter (Trader Joe's dupe)
note: An emulsified cream with coconut, shea, aloe and vitamin E, like the TJ body butter, so it sinks in rather than sitting greasy. Make it like the hand cream: two heated phases, then vitamin E and preservative below 40°C.

name: Coconut lemongrass body oil (TJ-style)
note: Copies the TJ oil blend: virgin coconut, olive, almond and jojoba with lemongrass. Lemongrass is kept to 0.6% because its citral can sensitize skin; the store bottle doesn't say how much it uses. Contains almond.

name: Almond ginger oatmeal soap (melt and pour)
note: A melt-and-pour take on the TJ French-milled bar. Colloidal oats give a soft polish; ginger and almond scent come from a skin-safe fragrance oil plus a few drops of ginger oil.

name: Guava honey lip butter
note: A nod to the TJ guava honey lip butter. Honey beads in wax, so stir as it cools, or use a lip-safe guava flavor oil instead.

name: Turmeric salt scrub (Kuu Spa-style)
note: Thai spa turmeric salt scrubs, made at home. Stir the turmeric into the oil, then mix in the salt. Scoop with a dry spoon and rub gently onto damp skin in the shower, then rinse. Body only, once or twice a week, and not on freshly shaved or broken skin, where salt stings. Turmeric can tint skin and grout yellow briefly. Skin looks smoother and brighter from exfoliating; it doesn't whiten or lighten.

name: Sandalwood chip tincture
note: Crush the chips or use powder in a glass jar and cover with perfumer's alcohol. Shake every day and keep somewhere dark for 4 to 8 weeks, then strain through a coffee filter. It's soft; layer it with vanilla tincture or a drop of sandalwood essential oil for more depth. Spray on clothes, hair ends or pulse points, not the face.

name: Seed-infused growth oil (Milagro-style)
note: As posted: peppercorn, black sesame and fenugreek seeds steeped in oil with a mint scent. The base oil isn't named, so sesame and castor are used here. Put the dry seeds in a clean, dry jar, cover with oil and leave 2 to 6 weeks out of the sun, shaking now and then, then strain. Dry seeds are fine to steep long; never add fresh or wet herbs. Massage a few drops into the scalp, not daily. The pepper tingle is irritation; stop if your scalp burns or flakes.

name: Seed-infused hair oil (gentler)
note: Safer version: the peppercorns are swapped for dried rosemary and the mint is halved, so there's less scalp irritation. Steep and strain the same way. Length retention comes mostly from handling: protective styles, trimming split ends and oiling the ends, not the seeds. Washing only once a month suits some hair, but if your scalp itches or flakes, wash more often.

name: Flaxseed curl gel (3 cups water)
note: Boil the water, add the flaxseed, simmer on low 10 minutes and strain while hot through a fine sieve or stocking (it's impossible to strain once cool). Makes about 2 cups. Keep in the fridge and use within 1 week; throw it out if it smells sour or goes cloudy and watery. Freeze some in an ice-cube tray to make it last.

name: Caffeine scalp tonic (Reedle-style)
claim: Cooling scalp serum for thinning hair
note: A homemade take on Korean brush-on scalp serums, minus the PDRN and exosomes. Warm the green tea, dissolve the caffeine, panthenol and niacinamide, cool, then add the glycerin and Geogard. Part hair and apply a few drops along the parts, massaging with fingertips or a silicone scalp brush. Use daily on a clean scalp. Topical caffeine has small studies for shedding, not regrowth; for real hair loss, minoxidil or a dermatologist does more.

name: Mellow leave-in hair cream (Anaze-style)
note: Inspired by Anaze Mellow Cream (coconut oil, royal jelly). Melt BTMS and coconut oil in a heatproof cup; heat the water separately to the same temperature, pour in and blend 1 minute. Cool, then stir in glycerin, panthenol, honey and Geogard. Honey stands in for royal jelly. Rub a pea-sized amount through damp mid-lengths and ends before blow-drying.

name: Beef marrow pre-shampoo hair butter (tutano)
claim: Stronger, softer curly and coily hair
note: The Brazilian tutano treatment, with amounts filled in. Roast marrow bones, scoop out the marrow and melt it on very low heat, then strain through a cloth until clear. Stir in the castor oil and rosemary while warm, pour into a jar and refrigerate. Warm a spoonful in your hands and work it into dry lengths and ends, not the scalp, for 30 to 40 minutes, then shampoo twice. It works like any rich fat: it coats hair and cuts breakage. Skip it with fine hair or an oily scalp, and throw it out if it smells sour. Use within 1 month.

name: Plant butter pre-shampoo (tutano alternative)
note: A vegetarian swap with a similar rich feel. Melt the butters, stir in the oils, and let it set. Use the same way: dry lengths for 30 minutes before shampoo. It keeps for months at room temperature.

name: Neem, clove and peroxide mouthwash (as posted)
note: As posted: 14 oz water, baking soda, 1 tbsp 3% hydrogen peroxide, neem, pine bark, cloves and cinnamon, steeped in the fridge 48 hours, then strained. Unpreserved herb water can grow bacteria in that time, so steep it overnight instead, strain, and use within a day. Diluted like this, peroxide is mild, but it breaks down within a day or two when mixed with plant material, so it adds little. Swish 30 seconds and spit; don't swallow. Daily peroxide rinses for weeks can irritate gums and stain the tongue.

name: Neem and clove herbal mouthwash (gentler)
note: Safer version: the peroxide is left out and xylitol added, which cavity bacteria can't feed on. Pour just-boiled water over the herbs, steep until cool, strain, then dissolve the baking soda and xylitol. Keep in the fridge and use within a day (a small batch, about 8 rinses). Swish and spit. Use it after brushing with fluoride or hydroxyapatite toothpaste, not instead.

name: Xylitol and hydroxyapatite rinse (non-toxic mouthwash)
note: Built from the "non-toxic mouthwash" list: xylitol, aloe, Dead Sea salt, holy basil and hydroxyapatite. Brew the tulsi in just-boiled water, strain and cool, then stir in the rest. Hydroxyapatite doesn't dissolve, so shake before each use. Swish 30 to 60 seconds after brushing and spit, and don't rinse with water afterward. Keep in the fridge and use within a day; with no preservative it spoils fast, so make a small batch.

name: Immortelle face oil (L'Occitane Divine-inspired)
claim: Smoother lines and a more even glow
note: The oils from the $120 Immortelle Divine Cream (evening primrose, sunflower and helichrysum), without the water, preservatives and fragrance allergens. Press 3 to 4 drops into damp skin at night, over a moisturizer if you're dry. Helichrysum is expensive and often faked, so buy from a seller with a GC/MS report. For real wrinkle and spot results, a retinoid and daily sunscreen do far more.

name: Shade-matched setting powder (Suppin-style)
claim: Soft-matte, blurred skin with no white cast
note: A homemade loose powder inspired by Japanese Club Suppin powder, which is known to leave a white cast on medium to deep skin. Sift the arrowroot, then add cocoa a pinch at a time until it disappears on your jaw. Deeper shades may need 1 tbsp or more. Dust on with a fluffy brush. Use a clean brush, keep it dry, and make a new batch every 3 months. Wearing powder to bed is fine for most people, but wash it off if you get breakouts.

name: Immortelle Divine face oil (dupe)
note: Built from L'Occitane's $120 Immortelle Divine Face Oil list: its first two ingredients are caprylic triglyceride and sunflower oil, followed by squalane, borage, argan, rosehip, primrose and sea buckthorn, with helichrysum and geranium for scent. This version skips the orange oil and keeps geranium very low. Press 3 to 4 drops into skin at night. Sea buckthorn tints orange, so 1 drop is enough. Store dark and cool, use within 6 months.

name: Verbena cooling body gel (L'Occitane-style)
claim: Light, citrusy gel that cools hot skin
note: Inspired by L'Occitane Verbena Cooling Gel. Brew lemon verbena leaves in just-boiled water for 10 minutes, strain and cool. Mix in glycerin and aloe, sprinkle xanthan while whisking until it gels, then add Geogard and litsea. Keep in the fridge for an extra cooling feel. The original has lemon peel oil, which can cause sun spots, and denatured alcohol; this skips both. Use within 2 months.

name: Overnight skin powder, unscented (Suppin-style)
claim: Soft-matte skin and less shine, even overnight
note: Closer to Club Suppin's formula: starch to absorb oil (their aluminum starch octenylsuccinate), a stearate so it clings like their zinc myristate, and silk or sericite for the blurred finish.
