Sift everything together twice. Add cocoa a pinch at a time to match your skin tone and avoid the white cast Suppin is known for. Dust lightly with a clean, fluffy brush. Unscented on purpose: perfumed powder sitting on skin all night is the most likely part to irritate. The hyaluronic acid and collagen in the original are tiny amounts and don't do much in a dry powder. Keep it dry and make a new batch every 3 months.

name: Almond supple skin oil (L'Occitane-style)
note: Built from L'Occitane's Almond Supple Skin Oil list: sweet almond and caprylic triglyceride first, then carrot, rosehip, sunflower and sea buckthorn. Theirs puts fragrance third; this version uses a few drops of vanilla instead and skips the bergamot and lemon peel oils, which can cause sun spots. Massage into damp skin after a shower. It softens skin; no oil firms it. Not for nut allergies.

name: Almond shower oil (L'Occitane-style)
claim: Cleanses and leaves skin soft, not tight
note: Shower oils are oil plus an emulsifier that turns milky with water and rinses off. Shake, pour into wet hands, massage over damp skin, then rinse. The oil makes the shower floor slippery, so rinse it off the tub. Best for dry skin; it cleans gently but won't remove heavy sunscreen as well as a gel.

name: Chalk tooth paste (1910 Club-style)
claim: Polishes off stains, fresh mint taste
note: Built like early-1900s Japanese toothpastes such as Club Toothpaste: chalk to polish, glycerin to make a paste, a little soap for light foam, and mint. Xylitol replaces saccharin; it sweetens and cavity bacteria can't feed on it. Clove oil is left out because it's harsh on gums when used daily. Stir the powders together, then mix in the glycerin, soap and peppermint until smooth. Scoop with a clean spatula. It has no fluoride, so use it alongside a fluoride or hydroxyapatite toothpaste, not instead.

name: Hibiscus scrub balls (as posted)
claim: Exfoliates and softens; pink, floral glow
note: As posted, with amounts filled in. Melt the shea and coconut, stir in almond oil, then the hibiscus powder and cornstarch, then the sugar, rose water and lavender. Press into balls and chill until firm. Rub one over damp skin in the shower and rinse; body only. The rose water adds water to a stored scrub with no preservative, so it can grow mold within a week or two, especially in a steamy bathroom. Hibiscus can tint skin and tubs pink briefly.

name: Hibiscus scrub balls (keeps for months)
claim: Same scrub balls, no mold risk
note: Safer version: the rose water is left out so the balls stay water-free, and a little extra shea holds them together. Make as above, press into balls (about 2 tbsp each), chill 30 minutes, then store in a dry jar outside the shower. Take one ball in with dry hands each time. For the rose scent, add 2 drops of geranium or use rose-scented fragrance oil. Body only; skip freshly shaved or broken skin.

name: Coconut vanilla dusting powder (Lush Coconut Drench-style)
claim: Soft, lightly scented skin and less chafing
note: Built from Lush's Coconut Drench list: corn and tapioca starch first, then coconut and a tonka-vanilla scent with vetiver. Sift the starches and coconut milk powder together. Drop the vanilla and vetiver onto a spoonful of the powder, rub it in with your fingers, then sift it back through the rest so there are no oily clumps. Leave it in a closed jar for 2 days so the scent spreads. Dust onto fully dry skin after a shower, on thighs, underarms or under the breasts. Don't shake it near a baby's face, and avoid breathing in the cloud. Keep the lid on and use within 6 months.

name: Unscented talc-free body powder (anti-chafe)
claim: Keeps skin dry and stops rubbing, for sensitive skin
note: The plain version for sensitive skin, eczema, or anywhere you've reacted to scented powders. Store dusting powders (Youth Dew, Wind Song, Woods of Windsor) list talc and up to 15 fragrance allergens; this has neither. Sift together and dust onto dry skin with a puff or shaker jar. Not for use on babies' diaper area unless your doctor says so; a barrier cream works better there.

name: Cocoa butter dusting powder (Lush Silky Underwear-style)
claim: Silky skin that clothes slide over; less chafing
note: Built from Lush Silky Underwear's list: corn starch, kaolin and grated cocoa butter, scented with jasmine and vetiver. Chill the cocoa butter, grate it on the finest side of a grater, then rub it into the starch and kaolin with your fingertips until there are no lumps. Add the oils the same way and sift. Dust over skin after moisturizing or a massage. Cocoa butter melts at body heat, so store it somewhere cool. Use within 6 months.

name: Lavender bedtime dusting powder (Lush Sleepy Dust-style)
claim: Soft skin and a calming lavender scent at bedtime
note: Built from Lush Sleepy Dust: tapioca, chamomile, lavender flower powder and lavender oil. This version leaves out the baking soda (it's alkaline and can sting sensitive skin and underarms) and the dyes. Grind dried lavender buds and chamomile to a fine powder in a spice grinder, sift out any rough bits, then mix with the tapioca and rub in the essential oil. Dust over skin before bed, or a pinch onto pillowcases. Lavender helps you wind down through its smell; it isn't a sleep treatment.

name: Corn-free sandalwood vanilla body powder (Merry Bath-style)
claim: Dry, soft skin with a light woody-sweet scent
note: Merry Bath's whole formula is arrowroot, kaolin, fragrance and aspen bark. This keeps the arrowroot and kaolin base (corn-free, for corn allergies) and swaps the fragrance oil for a few drops of real sandalwood and vanilla, so you know exactly what's in it. The aspen bark is left out: a dry powder doesn't need a preservative. Rub the oils into a spoonful of powder, sift through the rest, and let it rest closed for 2 days. Dust onto fully dry skin with a puff. Keep it lidded and dry; use within 6 months.

name: Honey leg massage (mustard-free wrap alternative)
claim: Smoother-feeling legs and a relaxing self-massage
note: A safer swap for the TikTok honey-mustard leg wrap. Warm the honey and oil together, smooth over clean, dry legs, then massage upward from ankles to thighs for 5 to 10 minutes. Honey gets tacky; the pulling and patting is a light lymphatic-style massage that can ease the puffy, heavy-leg feeling for a while. Rinse off in a warm shower. It won't remove cellulite or fat. See a doctor for swelling in one leg, swelling with pain or redness, or swelling that doesn't go down overnight.

name: Talc-free English rose body powder (Yardley-style)
note: Yardley's perfumed talcs are talc, chalk, magnesium carbonate, fragrance and triclosan. This swaps talc for arrowroot and tapioca, leaves out triclosan (a restricted antibacterial) and uses real rose and geranium with a touch of sandalwood, the notes on Yardley's English Rose card. Rub the oils into a spoonful of powder, sift through the rest, and let it rest closed 2 days. Dust onto dry body skin after a shower, not the face. Use within 6 months.

name: Talc-free English lavender body powder (Yardley-style)
note: Built on Yardley English Lavender's scent card: lavender, rosemary, cedar and geranium. Tonka and oakmoss are left out because both are common fragrance allergens (coumarin and oakmoss are listed by law). Talc is replaced with starch and triclosan is left out. Make like the rose powder. Body only.

name: Gentleman's deodorizing body powder (Yardley Gold-style)
claim: Dry, fresh skin with a warm woody scent
note: For the Yardley Gold and Elegance talcs. Triclosan was their "deo factor"; here a little zinc oxide does the odor job instead (it's mild, low-irritant and used in diaper creams). Sandalwood, lavender and patchouli give the warm woody-powdery note. No talc. Rub oils into a spoonful of powder, sift, rest 2 days. Dust onto chest, back, feet and underarms; not the groin if you're prone to irritation.

name: Anti-chafe zinc body powder (Anti Monkey Butt-style, no baking soda)
claim: Stops friction and sweat rash on thighs and folds
note: Anti Monkey Butt is cornstarch, kaolin, calamine, baking soda, tricalcium phosphate and fragrance. Calamine is mostly zinc oxide, so zinc oxide stands in. The baking soda is left out (alkaline, stings sweaty and shaved skin) and so is the fragrance. Sift together and dust onto fully dry skin before activity. If a rash is red, itchy and spreading with a sharp edge, it may be fungal and needs an antifungal cream.

name: Unscented men's comfort powder (Happy Nuts-style)
claim: Keeps the groin dry and chafe-free
note: Happy Nuts' full list is tapioca, corn starch, aloe powder, allantoin, oat bran, coconut and almond oils, preservatives and fragrance. This keeps the starch base and the soothing allantoin, adds a little zinc oxide, and leaves out the fragrance and almond oil (nut allergy), which is the gentlest choice for the groin. Apply to fully dry skin. Powder helps prevent jock itch by keeping skin dry, but it doesn't treat it: an itchy, red, ring-edged rash needs an antifungal (clotrimazole, miconazole or terbinafine).

name: Talc-free lily of the valley body powder (Yardley-style, lilial-free)
claim: Fresh green-floral powder without banned ingredients
note: Yardley's UK Lily of the Valley talc lists butylphenyl methylpropional (lilial), which has been banned in UK and EU cosmetics since 2022 because it may harm fertility; older stock and grey-market imports can still have it. There's no natural lily of the valley oil, so use a skin-safe fragrance oil labeled lilial-free, or a light geranium and bergamot FCF blend for a fresh floral. Talc is replaced with starch. Rub scent into a spoonful of powder, sift, rest 2 days. Body only.

name: Charcoal underarm bar (Kaia Takesumi-style, melt and pour)
note: Built from Kaia's underarm bar: activated charcoal, sea salt, shea, coconut, spearmint and rosemary. Apple cider vinegar is left out: in soap it's neutralized and does nothing. Melt the soap base, stir in shea, then charcoal and salt, cool slightly, add the oils and pour. Lather underarms for 30 seconds and rinse. Any soap washes away odor bacteria; charcoal doesn't "detox" or pull buildup from pores, but the bar works fine as a deodorant-switch wash. Charcoal can grey towels.

name: Unscented shave soap (Kitsch Shave Butter-style, melt and pour)
claim: Slick lather for a smoother shave
note: Kitsch's Shave Butter bar is sold as "irritation-free" but lists fragrance, lemon peel oil, camphor, coumarin, citral and limonene, all common irritants on freshly shaved skin. This keeps the shea and soap base and leaves the scent out. Melt the base, stir in shea and kaolin (kaolin gives the lather slip), pour. Lather onto wet skin, shave, rinse.

name: Lace Satin solid perfume (rose, jasmine, sandalwood)
claim: A pocket perfume without alcohol or phthalates
note: Yardley's Lace Satin body spray lists ethyl alcohol, butane propellants, diethyl phthalate and triclosan. This solid version keeps the rose-jasmine-sandalwood idea in beeswax and jojoba. Melt, cool slightly, stir in the oils, pour into a small tin. Dab onto wrists and neck. Use within a year.

name: Tart cherry solid body wash (Kitsch-style, melt and pour)
claim: Cleansing bar with a warm cherry-vanilla scent
note: Kitsch's Tart Cherry bar lists vanillin, coumarin, jasmine, cocoa, rose, rosemary, vitamin E and shea. This keeps the cocoa-shea base and the vanilla-rose-jasmine scent and leaves out coumarin, a listed fragrance allergen. For the cherry note, swap the drops for a skin-safe cherry fragrance oil. Melt the base, stir in shea and cocoa butter, cool to about 60°C, add vitamin E and the oils, pour and let set overnight.

name: Turmeric glow bar (Kitsch kojic bar alternative)
claim: Gentle cleansing bar with a natural golden color
note: Kitsch's kojic bar lists kojic acid, turmeric, ceramides, retinyl palmitate and tripeptide, but a wash rinses off in under a minute, so those actives barely work, and it adds citral, linalool and limonene. This keeps the turmeric and shea for color and softness and leaves out the actives and scent. Melt, stir in turmeric and shea, pour. It can tint towels yellow at first. For dark spots, use a leave-on azelaic acid, alpha arbutin or niacinamide serum instead.

name: Cucumber eucalyptus spa bar (Kitsch glycolic bar alternative)
note: Kitsch's glycolic bar pairs glycolic acid with shea, cucumber and eucalyptus. Acids don't work in soap: soap is alkaline and neutralizes them, so this skips the glycolic and keeps the spa feel. Kaolin gives a soft polish. Melt, stir in kaolin and shea, cool slightly, add the oils, pour. Keep eucalyptus products away from children under 6. For real smoothing, a leave-on glycolic or lactic acid lotion works far better.

name: Shea apricot exfoliating bar (Kitsch Shea Butter-style)
note: Kitsch's Shea Butter bar is soap made from sunflower and coconut oils, with shea, natural fragrance, salt, iron oxide, apricot seed powder and vitamin E. This keeps the shea and fine apricot scrub and leaves the fragrance out (a few drops of vanilla is fine). Melt, stir in shea and vitamin E, let it thicken slightly so the apricot powder doesn't sink, stir it in, pour. Body only; apricot powder is too rough for the face.

name: Tea tree and mint shampoo bar (Kitsch-style)
claim: Clarifies oily hair and buildup with a cooling feel
note: Kitsch's Tea Tree & Mint set: tea tree, mint and plant cleansers. Bars like this are mostly SCI, a mild sulfate-free cleanser. Wear a mask while handling SCI powder. Warm the SCI, butters and oils gently over a double boiler until soft and doughy, take off the heat, stir in the rest, press firmly into a mould and leave to harden 2 days. Rub on wet hair, lather, rinse. Dry it on a rack between uses so it lasts. Tea tree at this level is a refreshing scent, not a dandruff treatment; for real flakes use a ketoconazole, zinc pyrithione or selenium shampoo. Keep mint away from eyes and off children under 6.

name: Castor oil shampoo bar (Kitsch-style)
claim: Gentle, nourishing wash for dry hair
note: Kitsch's Castor Oil set lists castor, coconut, sunflower, olive, glycerin and pea extract with an amber-shea fragrance. Bars like this are mostly SCI, a mild sulfate-free cleanser. Wear a mask while handling SCI powder. Warm the SCI, butters and oils gently over a double boiler until soft and doughy, take off the heat, stir in the rest, press firmly into a mould and leave to harden 2 days. Rub on wet hair, lather, rinse. Dry it on a rack between uses so it lasts. Castor rinses off in seconds in a shampoo, so it won't grow hair; it just makes the lather creamier.

name: Coconut oil shampoo bar (Kitsch-style)
claim: Moisturizing wash for curly, coily and color-treated hair
note: Kitsch's Coconut Oil set: coconut, castor, olive, glycerin, with a white tea and coconut fragrance. Bars like this are mostly SCI, a mild sulfate-free cleanser. Wear a mask while handling SCI powder. Warm the SCI, butters and oils gently over a double boiler until soft and doughy, take off the heat, stir in the rest, press firmly into a mould and leave to harden 2 days. Rub on wet hair, lather, rinse. Dry it on a rack between uses so it lasts. Unscented or a few drops of vanilla keep it gentle.

name: Rice protein shampoo bar (Kitsch-style)
claim: Fuller-feeling fine, thin or damaged hair
note: Kitsch's Rice Water Protein set uses rice protein and vitamins B and C, scented with white tea and mandarin. Hydrolyzed rice protein is the part that actually helps: it coats damaged strands so they feel thicker. Real rice water can't go into a bar (it spoils), and vitamin C rinses off. Bars like this are mostly SCI, a mild sulfate-free cleanser. Wear a mask while handling SCI powder. Warm the SCI, butters and oils gently over a double boiler until soft and doughy, take off the heat, stir in the rest, press firmly into a mould and leave to harden 2 days. Rub on wet hair, lather, rinse. Dry it on a rack between uses so it lasts. If hair turns stiff, alternate with a moisture bar.

name: Rosemary and charcoal shampoo bar (Kitsch Rosemary & Biotin-style)
claim: Fresh, clean scalp and a volumizing wash
note: Kitsch's Rosemary & Biotin set lists biotin, amaranth, rosemary, oat peptide, castor and activated charcoal with lavender-vanilla scent. Biotin is left out: on hair it does nothing. Bars like this are mostly SCI, a mild sulfate-free cleanser. Wear a mask while handling SCI powder. Warm the SCI, butters and oils gently over a double boiler until soft and doughy, take off the heat, stir in the rest, press firmly into a mould and leave to harden 2 days. Rub on wet hair, lather, rinse. Dry it on a rack between uses so it lasts. Rosemary in a rinse-off bar is mostly scent; the rosemary-for-growth studies used leave-on oil for months. Charcoal can grey a white tub.

name: Ultra gentle unscented shampoo and body bar (Kitsch Ultra Sensitive-style)
claim: For sensitive skin and scalp, hair and body
note: Kitsch's Ultra Sensitive bar is castor, glycerin, coconut and shea, with no color or fragrance. Bars like this are mostly SCI, a mild sulfate-free cleanser. Wear a mask while handling SCI powder. Warm the SCI, butters and oils gently over a double boiler until soft and doughy, take off the heat, stir in the rest, press firmly into a mould and leave to harden 2 days. Rub on wet hair, lather, rinse. Dry it on a rack between uses so it lasts. The best pick for itchy, eczema-prone or reactive scalps, and safe for body washing.

name: Moisture conditioner bar (coconut and castor, Kitsch-style)
claim: Soft, detangled curly or dry hair
note: Matches Kitsch's coconut and castor conditioners. BTMS is what detangles. Melt everything except the panthenol and oils of scent over a double boiler, cool slightly, stir those in, pour into a mould and let set. Glide over wet lengths, not the scalp, then rinse.

name: Protein conditioner bar (rice, Kitsch-style)
claim: Strength and body for fine, damaged hair
note: Matches Kitsch's Rice Water Protein conditioner. Uses lighter oils so fine hair isn't weighed down. BTMS is what detangles. Melt everything except the panthenol and oils of scent over a double boiler, cool slightly, stir those in, pour into a mould and let set. Glide over wet lengths, not the scalp, then rinse.

name: Unscented conditioner and shave bar (Kitsch Ultra Sensitive-style)
claim: Detangles hair and gives razor glide, no fragrance
note: Kitsch's Ultra Sensitive conditioner doubles as a shave bar. BTMS is what detangles. Melt everything except the panthenol and oils of scent over a double boiler, cool slightly, stir those in, pour into a mould and let set. Glide over wet lengths, not the scalp, then rinse. To shave, rub onto wet legs or underarms and shave through the slip.

name: Vanilla oatmeal body powder (talc-free, corn-free)
claim: Soft, soothed, dry skin with a warm vanilla scent
note: KVK Naturals' vanilla oatmeal powder is the Merry Bath formula: arrowroot, kaolin, fragrance and aspen bark. This adds real colloidal oatmeal, which soothes itchy, dry skin, and swaps the fragrance for vanilla. Sift twice so the oats are fine. Dust onto dry skin. Good for corn allergy.

name: Gourmand dusting powder base (BathTreatBakery-style)
claim: Silky, scented body powder that helps stop thigh chafing
note: BathTreatBakery's whole range (40+ scents) is the same four ingredients: tapioca, arrowroot, kaolin and fragrance. Only the fragrance changes. This is that base; pick any blend from Make → Scent pairs (Powder) for skin-safe drops, or leave it unscented. Rub the oils into a spoonful of powder, sift through the rest, rest closed 2 days. Dust onto fully dry skin, or over body oil for scent layering. Powder absorbs moisture; it doesn't "lock it in".

name: Layering body oil (gourmand, jojoba and avocado)
claim: Glowy skin and a longer-lasting scent under powder
note: Like BathTreatBakery's Beautiful Glow body oils (jojoba or avocado oil plus fragrance). Use the same scent as your powder so they layer. Massage onto damp skin after a shower, let it sink in a few minutes, then dust powder over. Keep scent at 1% or less for all-day wear; skip cinnamon and clove oils.

name: Honey and shea soap (melt and pour)
note: As posted, with amounts: melt the soap base and shea together, take off the heat, then stir in the honey and pour. Keep honey to about 1 tsp per 200 g; more makes a sticky, sweaty bar that can scorch brown. Add it once the base cools to about 60°C. Let it set a few hours, then wrap in plastic so it doesn't sweat. Honey's "healing" effect mostly rinses off, but it gives a creamy, softer-feeling lather.

name: Jamaican-style hair growth mask (as posted)
note: As posted: 3 spoons coconut oil, 1 sweet potato, 2 eggs, 2 avocados, ½ banana, blended. Apply to clean, damp hair for 20 to 30 minutes, then rinse with cool water (hot water cooks egg into the hair) and shampoo. Banana and avocado bits are very hard to rinse out, so blend until totally smooth or strain. Make it fresh and use it all; raw egg carries salmonella, so wash hands and surfaces. It softens and coats hair; food masks don't make hair grow faster.

name: Avocado and banana softening mask (no egg, easy rinse)
claim: Soft, moisturized hair after one use
note: Safer version: no raw egg and a smaller, smoother batch that rinses out. Blend until silky with no lumps, add a spoon of conditioner to help it slip out. Leave 20 minutes, rinse well, then condition. Coconut oil reduces protein loss in washing; avocado and banana add slip and softness. For real length, protect ends and cut breakage.

name: Panthenol hair booster (Bepantol-style)
claim: Softer, more elastic curls and less breakage
note: Bepantol Derma liquid is mostly panthenol (vitamin B5) in water. Most people mix a few drops into their leave-in or a spray bottle. This makes a 5% spray: dissolve panthenol in warm water, add glycerin and Geogard. Mist onto damp hair and scrunch, or add 1 tsp to a handful of leave-in. Panthenol genuinely helps hair hold moisture and bend without snapping; it doesn't grow hair.

name: Rose witch hazel face mist (Dollar Tree Dermasil-style)
claim: Refreshing mist that balances oily skin
note: Copies the Dermasil Balancing spray idea. Use alcohol-free witch hazel. Mix, add Geogard, shake. Mist over skin and pat in, then moisturize. It's mostly water, so it refreshes rather than treats; the store version at $1.25 is a fine buy if the list is short and fragrance-light.

name: Aloe calendula face and body mist
claim: Soothing mist for dry or sensitive skin
note: Like Dermasil's Soothing and Nourishing sprays, without the lavender oil (a common irritant on the face). Steep dried calendula in just-boiled water 15 minutes, strain and cool, then add the rest and shake. Use within 2 months.

name: Bentonite and turmeric face mask (as posted)
note: As posted, with amounts filled in. Mix in a non-metal bowl into a smooth paste. Apply a thin layer and rinse after 10 to 15 minutes, before it cracks fully dry; clay left to crack pulls moisture out. Turmeric can tint skin yellow for a few hours, especially lighter skin. Once a week for oily skin. It absorbs oil and leaves skin looking fresher; it won't lighten skin, remove dark spots or clear acne on its own.

name: Gentle clay and turmeric mask (dry or sensitive skin)
note: Safer version: kaolin is gentler than bentonite, honey and yogurt keep it from drying out, and the turmeric is just a pinch so it won't stain. Mix, apply, rinse after 10 minutes. Patch test turmeric first; some people react to it.

name: Neem, sulfur and tea tree soap (as posted)
claim: Antibacterial bar for acne and body odor
note: As posted, with amounts: mix neem and sulfur powder into the tea tree oil, then stir into melted base and pour. Stir as it thickens, or the heavy powders sink to the bottom (the creator saw this too). Sulfur smells like matches until it cures. It's a good body wash for oily, acne-prone backs and chests, and helps with dandruff on the body. Rinse-off time is short, so for facial acne a leave-on sulfur or benzoyl peroxide product does more.

name: Coconut honey brown sugar scrub (as posted)
note: As posted, with amounts. The body wash makes it lather and rinse clean. It turns watery over time because the honey and wash separate from the oil; stir before each use. Scoop with a dry spoon and keep shower water out. Body only.

name: Rose and calendula body oil (as posted)
note: As posted: dried rose petals and calendula steeped in almond oil, then strained and vitamin E added. 24 hours gives a light infusion; 1 to 2 weeks in a warm, dark place gives more color, as one commenter does. Use only fully dried petals; fresh ones add water and mold. Strain well. Not for nut allergies.

name: Rose clay and beetroot soap (as posted)
note: As posted, with amounts: mix rose clay and beetroot powder into a little rose water, stir into the melted base, pour. Beetroot's pink fades and can turn brown over a few weeks in soap; rose clay holds color better. It can tint the lather pink at first.

name: Lemon turmeric glow oil (as posted)
note: As posted: fresh lemon peel and turmeric steeped in sunflower oil for 24 hours, then strained. Two problems: lemon peel releases compounds that cause dark patches and burns in the sun on leave-on skin, and fresh peel adds water that can grow mold in oil. Turmeric stains clothes and skin yellow.

name: Turmeric glow oil (sun-safe)
note: Safer version: no lemon peel. Warm turmeric in the oil gently for 20 minutes, let settle overnight and pour off the clear oil (or strain through a coffee filter) so it doesn't stain. For a citrus scent, use bergamot FCF, which won't cause sun spots. Glow comes from the oil; turmeric adds color.

name: Grapeseed oil soap with green color (as posted)
note: As posted. Keep grapeseed to about 1 tsp per 200 g, or the bar sweats oil and lathers poorly. Use soap-safe colorant rather than food coloring, which bleeds and tints skin; spirulina or green clay give a natural green.

name: Green clay and grapeseed soap
note: Safer version: green clay instead of food dye, so no bleeding or staining. Mix clay into a little of the melted base first to avoid clumps, then stir in and pour.

name: Turmeric and lemon sugar scrub (as posted)
note: As posted: sugar, turmeric, the lemon turmeric oil, lemon juice and body wash. Lemon juice adds water (so a stored jar can mold) and the lemon oil can cause dark marks if any stays on skin in the sun. Body only.

name: Turmeric sugar scrub (no lemon)
note: Safer version: no lemon juice or peel, so it keeps and won't cause sun marks. Use the sun-safe turmeric glow oil or plain sunflower oil. For lather, add a squeeze of body wash to each handful as you use it rather than to the jar, which keeps the jar from separating. Scoop with a dry spoon; body only; can tint the tub.

name: Honey herbal face mask (as posted)
note: As posted, with amounts: honey with neem, beetroot, coffee, turmeric and rose powders. Smooth on (don't scrub with the coffee), leave 10 to 15 minutes, rinse with lukewarm water. Beetroot and turmeric can tint skin pink-yellow for a few hours. Make it fresh each time.

name: Chamomile rose toner (as posted)
note: As posted: chamomile and rose petals soaked in rose water for 24 hours, strained, then glycerin and lavender added and stored in a spray bottle. With no preservative, herb-soaked water can grow bacteria within days.

name: Chamomile rose toner (preserved)
note: Safer version: steep the herbs in just-boiled water for 15 minutes (heat extracts better than 24 hours cold and reduces germs), strain through a coffee filter, then add rose water, glycerin and Geogard. Lavender is left out because it often irritates the face. Use within 2 months.

name: Bentonite, vinegar and glycolic dandruff mask (as posted)
note: As posted, with amounts: bentonite clay, apple cider vinegar and Sadoer 7% Glycolic + Ceramide toner, applied to the scalp. Undiluted vinegar plus an acid toner on the scalp can sting, burn and irritate, especially with scratched or broken skin. Clay and acids can lift loose flakes for a few days, but most dandruff is caused by a yeast, which this doesn't treat.

name: Gentle clay scalp mask for flakes
claim: Lifts flakes and calms an oily, itchy scalp
note: Safer version: clay mixed with water and a little aloe, with a few drops of tea tree. No acid toner or vinegar. Part hair, apply to the scalp, leave 10 minutes (don't let it dry hard), rinse well and shampoo. Use once a week. For dandruff that keeps coming back, use a shampoo with ketoconazole, zinc pyrithione or selenium sulfide, left on 5 minutes, 2 to 3 times a week; a home mask can't replace that.

name: Sugar wax with glycerin (as posted)
note: As posted, with amounts: sugar, lemon juice and water cooked 10 to 15 minutes to golden, cooled, then a little glycerin stirred in to keep it pliable. Glycerin isn't needed: it makes the paste softer and less grippy and can leave skin sticky. If your wax sets too hard, rewarm it briefly or cook it a minute less next time instead. The three-ingredient sugar wax in the library is the safer version. Hot sugar burns badly, so let it cool to warm before touching, test on your inner wrist first, and keep it off broken or sunburned skin.

name: Moringa sugar scrub (as posted)
note: As posted, with amounts. Moringa gives a green color and a grassy smell. Body wash in the jar separates over time, so stir before use, or add a squeeze of wash to each handful instead. Scoop with a dry spoon; body only.

name: Hibiscus and lavender body scrub (as posted)
note: As posted: lavender buds steeped in almond oil 3 to 4 hours and strained, then hibiscus, sugar, lavender oil and body wash mixed in. A few hours gives a light scent; dried buds can steep for days. Hibiscus may tint the tub pink. Body only; not for nut allergies.

name: Turmeric lip balm (as posted)
note: As posted, with amounts. Use only a pinch of turmeric; more stains lips and teeth yellow and feels gritty. Stir as it cools so the turmeric doesn't sink. Patch test; some people react to turmeric on lips. For a reliable tint, a pinch of beetroot powder or cocoa works too.

name: Ayurvedic herbal hair rinse (sage, rosemary, brahmi, ginger)
claim: Postpartum ritual for strong, shiny hair
note: From a 40-day Ayurvedic postpartum routine. Simmer the herbs in the water for 10 minutes, steep 20, strain well and cool to lukewarm. Pour over clean hair as a final rinse. It adds shine and a nice scent; it can't stop postpartum shedding, which is normal and settles by about a year. Make it fresh each time; a herbal water spoils within a day. Keep ginger to a pinch, as it tingles on the scalp.

name: Ayurvedic herb hair mask (amla, bhringraj, brahmi, hibiscus)
note: Based on the classic herb set sold for postpartum hair. Mix the powders with aloe and warm water into a yogurt-thick paste, apply to damp hair and scalp, leave 20 to 30 minutes, then rinse very well and condition. Herbs condition and add slip; they can't stop postpartum shedding. Fenugreek is related to peanuts and chickpeas, so leave it out if you react to legumes. Hibiscus can tint light hair pinkish. Mix fresh each time.

name: Royal saffron milk bath
claim: The Mughal and Rajasthani court ritual for soft, glowing skin
note: Steep the saffron in a cup of warm milk for 15 minutes until golden, add the rest of the milk, and pour into a warm bath. Soak 15 to 20 minutes, then rinse. The softness comes from the milk's fats and natural lactic acid; saffron adds color, scent and ceremony. A pinch is plenty, as it stains the tub and skin yellow at higher amounts. Skip it if you're allergic to dairy.

name: Avocado deep conditioner (as posted, stored in a jar)
claim: Blend, jar it, and keep for later
note: As posted. Fresh avocado, coconut cream and aloe are food and water with no preservative, so a jar of this grows bacteria and mold within a day or two, even before you can see or smell it. Use the make-fresh version instead.

name: Avocado deep conditioner (make fresh)
note: One treatment. Blend until completely smooth (lumps of avocado are hard to rinse out), apply to damp hair from mid-lengths to ends, cover with a shower cap for 20 to 30 minutes, then rinse well and shampoo lightly if it feels heavy. Use olive oil for fine hair; swap in 1 tsp castor oil for thick, dry hair. Throw away what's left; to save time, freeze single portions in an ice cube tray for up to a month and thaw in the fridge.

name: Horsetail, rosemary and peppermint hair oil
claim: Scalp oil for stronger, faster-growing hair
note: Warm the dried horsetail and rosemary in the oil on the lowest heat or in a water bath for 1 to 2 hours, never frying. Cool, strain through a coffee filter so no plant bits remain, then add the peppermint oil. Massage a few drops into the scalp 2 or 3 times a week. Peppermint gives the tingle; keep it away from eyes and skip it for children under 6. Rosemary and horsetail growth claims rest on weak evidence; the massage and oil help the scalp feel cared for.

name: Rosemary soapnut shampoo (with Cosgard)
note: Simmer the soapnuts and rosemary in the water for 15 minutes, cool and strain well, then measure 80 g of the tea. Stir it into the shampoo base with the glycerin, and add Cosgard last at 1% of the total. This is well built: adding tea dilutes the base's own preservative, and the Cosgard covers that. Check the pH is under 6 with a strip if you can. Keeps about 3 months; bin it if it smells off or separates.

name: Coffee and honey scalp mask
note: Mix used coffee grounds with honey, massage gently into the scalp, leave 20 to 30 minutes and rinse well. It feels invigorating and lightly exfoliating, and the honey softens. Caffeine growth studies used leave-on tonics, not a 20-minute mask, so expect a nice scalp treat rather than faster growth. Grounds cling to thick or curly hair; rinse thoroughly and use a drain catcher.

name: Golden flaxseed and amla hair mask
claim: Softer hair and easier detangling on wash day
note: Simmer the flaxseeds in the water for 10 minutes, stirring, until it turns slippery. Strain hot through a stocking or fine sieve, let it cool, then stir in the amla oil. Apply to sectioned, damp hair for 15 to 30 minutes and rinse well. Flaxseed gel gives slip and softness; amla oil adds shine. Keep the rest in the fridge for up to 5 days, or freeze in an ice cube tray.

name: Minty sea breeze body bar (DIY)
claim: That cool, tingly 'clean' feeling of the viral Sea Breeze bar
note: Inspired by the viral Dollar Tree Sea Breeze bar, without trying to copy it. Melt the base, stir in the kaolin until smooth, cool to about 60°C, add the oils, pour and let set overnight. Peppermint and eucalyptus give the cooling tingle; kaolin gives a clean, slightly matte feel. Body and hands only: keep it off the face and away from eyes, and skip it for children under 6. A tingle is a cooling sensation, not a sign it's cleaning better.

name: Minty crystal salt scrub (like Lush Magic Crystals)
claim: Scrubs and cleanses with a cool mint tingle
note: Lush's version is mostly Epsom and sea salt held in a foaming cleanser (SLES) with mint oils and menthol. Stir the salts into the liquid shampoo base, then add the oils and menthol dissolved in a teaspoon of the base. It's a scrub and a wash in one: rub a handful over wet skin and rinse. Body only, never on freshly shaved skin or the face, and keep it away from eyes and children under 6. Water-free apart from the preserved base, so keep shower water out of the jar.

name: Cooling body conditioner bar (like Lush Tingle)
claim: Soft, minty skin straight out of the shower
note: An in-shower body conditioner: after washing, rub over wet skin, then rinse lightly. Lush's Tingle uses jojoba, murumuru and shea with menthol and mint oils (it also carries cassia leaf oil and cinnamal, common allergens, which this version leaves out). Melt everything except the peppermint, cool slightly, add the oil and pour into a mould. The Olivem lets it rinse off milky instead of greasy. Water-free, so no preservative is needed; keep it dry between uses. Body only.

name: Calming oat cleansing balm (like Lush Sleepy Face)
claim: Melts off makeup and leaves skin soft at night
note: Lush's version is cocoa, shea and illipe butters with jojoba, almond oil, oat and lavender. Melt the butters on low, stir in the oils and oat, cool slightly, add the lavender and pour into a tin. Sweep over dry skin, massage, then wipe off with a warm damp cloth. Water-free, so no preservative is needed; keep water out of the tin. Like the original, it softens at body heat, so store it somewhere cool. Skip the lavender for very sensitive skin.

name: Almond and kaolin powder cleanser (like Lush Angels on Bare Skin)
note: Lush's version is ground almonds, glycerin, kaolin and water with lavender, rose and chamomile. This keeps it dry instead, so nothing can grow in the jar: grind the flowers fine, mix everything and store with the lid on. To use, tip a pinch into your palm with a few drops of water (and a drop of glycerin if you like), make a paste, massage over damp skin and rinse. Press lightly; it is a polish, not a scrub. Tree nut: skip with a nut allergy.

name: Linseed and aloe multi-use cream (like Lush's linseed cream)
claim: Light moisturiser, shaving cream and hair-ends smoother in one
note: Lush's version calls itself self-preserving but contains drying alcohol, propylene glycol and benzyl alcohol, which do that job. Homemade, a preservative does it. Simmer the flaxseed in the water 10 minutes and strain. Heat the flax water with the aloe and glycerin, and separately the oils with the Olivem, both to about 70 C. Pour oils into water while blending, cool below 40 C, then add honey and Cosgard. Pat on after shaving, use as a shaving cream, or work a little through dry ends.

name: Rosemary coconut hair butter (as posted)
claim: Pre-shampoo that protects hair and helps it grow
note: As posted on TikTok: warm the coconut oil and dried rosemary on low for 30 to 60 minutes without boiling, strain, and let it set. Apply before washing (from mid-lengths to ends if your roots are oily or your hair is fine), leave 40 minutes to 1 hour, then shampoo, twice if needed. Strain very well; leftover leaf bits can mould. Use a thermometer rather than your finger and keep it under about 80 C. It sets solid below about 24 C and melts in warm rooms; that is normal.

name: Minty herbal shower gel (like Lush Dirty Springwash)
note: Lush's version is an SLES shower gel with spearmint, peppermint, thyme and tarragon, plus blue colour. This starts from a ready-made, preserved unscented base, so there is nothing to cook or preserve: stir the glycerin and oils into the base, shake and leave a day for the scent to settle. Body only; keep mint off the face and away from children under 6.

name: Whipped oat shaving butter (like Lush Dirty shaving cream)
claim: Slick, cushioned shave that leaves skin soft
note: Lush's version is a creamy shave with shea, oat and fragrance (including coumarin and benzyl allergens). This one is fragrance-light. Melt the shea and coconut, stir in the almond oil and oat, chill until just firm, then whip with the shampoo base for a few minutes until fluffy. Smooth a thin layer on wet skin and shave with a sharp blade; rinse the razor often. The shampoo base is already preserved, and nothing else adds water, but keep the jar dry and scoop with a clean spoon.

name: Seven-oil dry body oil (like Nuxe Huile Prodigieuse)
claim: Satin, non-greasy glow for body, face and hair ends
note: The same seven oils Nuxe lists (camellia/tsubaki, argan, macadamia, borage, hazelnut, sweet almond), with caprylic/capric triglyceride doing what makes it 'dry': it spreads thin and absorbs fast. Neroli and sweet orange stand in for orange blossom, with a touch of vanilla and ylang for the magnolia-vanilla warmth. Mix everything in a clean, dry bottle with a fine-mist spray or a pump and shake. On damp skin right after the shower, it sinks in within a minute. For hair, rub 1 or 2 sprays between your palms and smooth over the ends, never the roots. No water, so no preservative; use within 6 to 9 months, kept away from heat and light. Tree nuts: skip with a nut allergy.

name: Fresh floral dry oil (like Nuxe Huile Prodigieuse Florale)
claim: Same satin oil, fresher grapefruit-floral scent
note: Same seven-oil base as the original; only the scent changes. Use steam-distilled or FCF grapefruit, because cold-pressed grapefruit oil can make skin burn in the sun. A synthetic white musk perfume oil gives the soft musky finish. Mix everything in a clean, dry bottle with a fine-mist spray or a pump and shake. On damp skin right after the shower, it sinks in within a minute. For hair, rub 1 or 2 sprays between your palms and smooth over the ends, never the roots. No water, so no preservative; use within 6 to 9 months, kept away from heat and light.

name: Rich dry oil for very dry skin (like Nuxe Huile Prodigieuse Riche)
claim: Comforting winter oil for rough elbows, shins and coarse hair
note: More macadamia and less of the light triglyceride, so it feels richer and leaves a cosier layer. Best on very dry or flaking skin, in winter, or as a pre-shampoo on thick, coarse hair. Too heavy for fine hair. Mix everything in a clean, dry bottle with a fine-mist spray or a pump and shake. On damp skin right after the shower, it sinks in within a minute. For hair, rub 1 or 2 sprays between your palms and smooth over the ends, never the roots. No water, so no preservative; use within 6 to 9 months, kept away from heat and light.

name: Gold or rose-gold shimmer dry oil (like Nuxe Huile Prodigieuse Or)
claim: Sun-kissed shimmer for collarbones, shins and hair tips
note: The seven-oil base plus fine cosmetic mica. Use gold mica with the original scent (like Or), or rose-gold mica with the grapefruit-floral scent (like Or Florale). Shake well before every use, since the mica settles. Keep it off the eyes, use a pump rather than a fine mist so you don't breathe in the powder, and buy mica from a seller who states ethical sourcing. On hair, a little on the ends only; too much looks dusty. Mix everything in a clean, dry bottle with a fine-mist spray or a pump and shake. On damp skin right after the shower, it sinks in within a minute. For hair, rub 1 or 2 sprays between your palms and smooth over the ends, never the roots. No water, so no preservative; use within 6 to 9 months, kept away from heat and light.

name: Plum and sesame night oil (like Nuxe Huile Prodigieuse Néroli)
claim: Ultra-light, soothing oil for sensitive skin and bedtime
note: Nuxe's Néroli version drops the seven oils for just two: plum kernel oil (light, almond-scented) and untoasted sesame oil (silky, fast-absorbing). Bergamot must be FCF (bergapten-free) for a leave-on oil; regular bergamot burns skin in the sun. Lavender stands in for lavandin. For very sensitive skin, leave the essential oils out completely; the plum oil smells lovely on its own. Light enough for fine hair. Mix everything in a clean, dry bottle with a fine-mist spray or a pump and shake. On damp skin right after the shower, it sinks in within a minute. For hair, rub 1 or 2 sprays between your palms and smooth over the ends, never the roots. No water, so no preservative; use within 6 to 9 months, kept away from heat and light.

name: Milky body toner (like Knock Melt In Body Toner)
claim: Light, fast-absorbing body hydration that holds perfume longer
note: A thin, pourable body milk rather than a lotion. Knock's version uses glycerin, squalane, ceramide NP, cholesterol and niacinamide; this keeps the same idea. Warm the water, glycerin, panthenol and niacinamide in one jug, and the squalane, Olivem and ceramide complex in another, both to about 70 C. Pour the oils into the water while blending, sprinkle in the xanthan, blend until smooth, cool below 40 C and add the Cosgard. Pour into a pump or flip-top bottle. Use on damp skin straight after the shower, then spray perfume on top: moisturised skin holds scent longer. Unscented on purpose so it never clashes with your perfume. Contains water, so the preservative is essential; use within 3 months.

name: Colour-correcting setting powder, green or pink (Suppin-style)
claim: Tones down redness (green) or brightens dullness (pink) while absorbing shine
note: Like Club Suppin's green and pink tins, using clay for the tint. Green clay neutralises redness; for a pink, brightening version, swap the green clay for the same amount of pink clay. Sift everything together twice so the colour is even, and store in a jar with a sifter lid. Press a thin layer on with a puff, mainly where you are shiny or red. Start with less clay; you can always add more. Clay is drying, so skip this over very dry patches. The tint is subtle and won't cover marks the way makeup does.

name: Burdock and nettle pre-wash scalp oil (like BUR BUR Growing Season)
claim: Softer scalp, fewer flakes and less breakage on wash day
note: BUR BUR infuses burdock root and nettle leaf in olive oil, then adds jojoba, squalane, bakuchiol and vitamin C. First infuse: warm the olive oil with the dried burdock and nettle on the lowest heat for 1 to 2 hours without letting it bubble, then strain very well through a coffee filter; leftover plant bits can mould. Stir in the jojoba, squalane, bakuchiol (warm gently until it dissolves), vitamin E and the oils, and store in a dark dropper bottle. Massage a few droppers into a dry scalp, pull the rest through the ends, leave 45 minutes to overnight, then shampoo twice. Once or twice a week. Hydrolyzed proteins dissolve in water, not oil, so they go in your conditioner, not here.

name: Rose jelly soap (as posted)
claim: Pretty rose soap that wobbles like jelly
note: As posted: melt the soap base, add glycerin and gelatin, put dried roses in the mould and pour over. Two problems. Melt-and-pour base already sets firm, so gelatin only works if you dissolve it in hot water first, and then the extra water makes the bar sweat and soften. Dried rose petals inside soap turn brown and slimy within days, so place only a few on top. Real jelly soap is made from liquid soap instead; see the version below.

name: Wobbly rose jelly soap (fridge)
claim: Bouncy, rose-scented jelly soap that actually wobbles
note: Sprinkle the gelatin over the cold water and leave 5 minutes to bloom, then warm gently, without boiling, until clear. Take off the heat, stir in the body wash slowly (whisking makes foam), add the pink clay for colour and the rose oil, then pour into silicone moulds. Press a few dried petals on top if you like. Chill 3 hours until set. Rub a piece between wet hands or on a loofah. Gelatin and water spoil, so keep the jellies in the fridge and use within 2 weeks. Vegan: use 1 g agar instead of the gelatin; it sets firmer and less bouncy.

name: Fried onion paste hair oil (as posted)
note: As posted: blend 2 onions to a paste, simmer in a cup of coconut or sesame oil for 20 to 30 minutes, strain and jar. The risk is water: 20 to 30 minutes often isn't enough to cook all the water out of fresh onion, and fresh vegetables kept in oil can grow mould and, in rare cases, botulism bacteria. Keep cooking until the paste is crisp and the bubbling stops completely, strain through a coffee filter, then keep it in the fridge and use within 2 weeks. The dried-onion version below avoids all of this.

name: Dried onion sesame hair oil (no fresh onion)
claim: Onion hair oil without the water or the spoilage risk
note: Dried onion flakes carry no water into the oil, so it keeps for months. Warm the sesame oil and onion flakes on the lowest heat for 30 minutes, cool, strain through a coffee filter, and stir in the castor oil and rosemary. Massage into the scalp, leave 1 to 2 hours, then shampoo. Twice a week. It still smells oniony; the rosemary and a second shampoo help. Patch test first, since onion can sting a scratched scalp.

name: Agarwood (oud) chip tincture
claim: A real, deep oud scent made at home
note: The safe home version of what the TikTok shows. Distilling oud oil needs a still and days of heat, and heating alcohol at home is a fire risk, so make a tincture instead. Grind the chips coarsely, cover with the perfumer's alcohol in a glass jar, and leave 4 to 8 weeks in a dark cupboard, shaking every few days. Filter through a coffee filter, then add the rose and sandalwood to round it out and leave 2 more weeks. Spray on clothes or wrists. Buy cultivated agarwood; wild trees are endangered.

name: Baobab shine oil (like LOMA Nourishing Oil, silicone-free)
claim: Light shine and softness for dry ends
note: LOMA's actual list starts with dimethicone, trisiloxane and isoparaffin (silicones and a solvent), with baobab and creatine further down, plus fragrance. This is the plant-oil version of what its marketing describes. Mix and store in a pump bottle. Rub 1 or 2 pumps between your palms and smooth over damp or dry ends. Not a heat protectant: no plant oil protects to 450 F, and oil on hot tools can sizzle. For heat styling, use a silicone heat spray and keep tools under about 180 C (350 F).

name: Calendula rosehip face oil (like Stokli)
claim: Calming, softening face, hand and body oil
note: Stokli's list is calendula, rosehips, jojoba and raspberry seed oil. Infuse the dried calendula in the jojoba on the lowest heat for 1 to 2 hours, strain through a coffee filter, then add the rosehip, raspberry seed oil and vitamin E. Press 3 or 4 drops onto damp skin at night. Rosehip and raspberry oils go rancid fast, so make small batches and keep them in the fridge or a cool dark place; bin it if it smells like crayons. Skip calendula if you react to daisies or ragweed.

name: 13-herb rice wine hair tonic (Loom Beauty, as posted)
claim: Less hair fall, new growth, fewer greys
note: As posted: arborvitae leaf, processed fo-ti, ginseng, eclipta (bhringraj), dong quai, Szechuan lovage, ku shen, glossy privet, red sage, drynaria, reishi and safflower, steeped in 65% rice spirit for 2 months. Amounts weren't given, so about 10 g each is assumed. Used straight, 65% alcohol stings and dries the scalp. Fo-ti and ku shen can irritate, and dong quai can make skin sun-sensitive. Dilute it before use (see the next recipe), patch test, and never drink it: fo-ti has caused liver injury taken by mouth.

name: Ginseng and arborvitae scalp tonic (diluted)
claim: A gentler leave-in scalp tonic in the same tradition
note: A simpler, safer take on the Vietnamese herbal tonic. It keeps the best-studied herbs (ginseng, arborvitae, rosemary, bhringraj) and drops fo-ti, ku shen and dong quai. Steep the herbs in the spirit for 4 weeks, shaking now and then, then strain through a coffee filter. Mix that tincture with the hydrosol, glycerin and Cosgard. At about 20% alcohol it barely stings, but that's too weak to keep microbes out on its own, so the Cosgard is there to make sure. Part your hair and spray onto the scalp, massage and leave in. Once a day or every other day. Skip broken or sunburnt skin.

name: Hibiscus, curry leaf and methi infused hair oil (Loom Beauty-style)
claim: Softer, shinier hair and a calmer scalp
note: Loom Beauty's second recipe: grapeseed oil, rosemary, hibiscus, curry leaf, neem leaf, lavender and methi, blended with almond, rice bran and castor oils; their video also adds ginger root and pomelo peel, then rosemary, tea tree and peppermint essential oils for scent. Dried ginger and pomelo peel work here too; skip fresh ones. Use only dried herbs; fresh leaves carry water that makes oil go mouldy. Warm the oils and herbs on the lowest heat for 1 to 2 hours (or leave in a sunny window for 2 to 4 weeks), then strain twice, the second time through a coffee filter. Massage into the scalp, leave 1 hour to overnight, and shampoo twice. Once or twice a week.

name: Fenugreek, amla and bhringraj hair butter (like Herbal Lineage)
claim: A whipped sealant for length retention on natural hair
note: The herbs go into the oil first, not straight into the butter, so the butter stays smooth instead of gritty. Warm the coconut and castor oils with the fenugreek, amla and bhringraj on the lowest heat for 1 hour, then strain through a fine cloth or coffee filter. Melt the shea and mango butters, stir in the herbal oil, chill until just firm at the edges, then whip for 5 minutes until fluffy. Use as the last step after a water-based leave-in (the LOC or LCO method): a small amount on the lengths and ends to seal in moisture. Length retention means less breakage, not faster growth. Fenugreek is a legume; skip it with a peanut or chickpea allergy.

name: Pomarrosa (rose apple) spray perfume
claim: The rosy, dewy smell of yellow rose apple, with a soft nutty base like its seed
note: Rose apple (Syzygium jambos, pomarrosa or manzana rosa) really does smell like rose water; the flesh contains some of the same scent molecules as roses. This builds it from natural oils. Top: steam-distilled grapefruit for the juicy, watery bite. Heart: rose with a little geranium, rosy and slightly green like the fruit skin; rose plus a citrus drop is the classic lychee trick. Base: sandalwood and vanilla for the seed's soft, nutty warmth, since bitter almond oil isn't safe. Mix the oils in a glass bottle, add the alcohol, shake, and let it rest 2 to 4 weeks in the dark. Spray on clothes or pulse points. For true green apple, pear or lychee, add 1 or 2 drops of a skin-safe fragrance oil; those notes have no essential oil. A homemade tincture of the fruit won't keep its scent: fresh fruit aroma fades and spoils in alcohol at home.

name: Berry musk body mist (like Candie's Berry Musk)
claim: Sweet berry, soft floral and vanilla-musk body mist
note: Candie's notes: strawberry and raspberry, then lily and violet leaf, then vanilla orchid, sandalwood and musk. Berry has no essential oil, so a few drops of a skin-safe berry fragrance oil give the top; geranium stands in for the rosy-green violet leaf and lily. Stir the oils into the polysorbate until clear, add the hydrosol and glycerin, then the Geogard last. Shake before each use. Mist over body and hair, not the face. Keeps 3 to 6 months. No UV filters needed: those are in store mists to protect the liquid's colour and scent in clear bottles, so use an opaque or dark bottle instead.

name: Mango lychee body mist (like Candie's)
claim: Juicy tropical fruit with soft white flowers and clean musk
note: Candie's notes: mango nectar and lychee, then honeysuckle and white peony, then white musk and cedarwood. Mango comes from a fragrance oil; rose with a drop of steam-distilled grapefruit gives the lychee, and a single drop of jasmine stands in for honeysuckle. Stir the oils into the polysorbate until clear, add the hydrosol and glycerin, then the Geogard last. Shake before each use. Mist over body and hair, not the face. Keeps 3 to 6 months.

name: Pink currant body mist (like Candie's)
claim: Tart berry, jasmine and cotton-candy vanilla body mist
note: Candie's notes: pink currant and amberwood, then pear blossom and night jasmine, then cotton candy musk and vanilla sugar. Blackcurrant comes from a fragrance oil; cedarwood gives the dry amberwood, and extra vanilla with musk makes the cotton-candy finish. Stir the oils into the polysorbate until clear, add the hydrosol and glycerin, then the Geogard last. Shake before each use. Mist over body and hair, not the face. Keeps 3 to 6 months.

name: Six-oil hair blend (as posted)
note: As posted: 1 oz each of jojoba, grapeseed, Cecred Hair Ritual Oil, pumpkin seed, coconut and castor. Cecred is a store-bought blend, so argan stands in here. Shake well; castor settles. Massage into the scalp and lengths, leave 1 hour to overnight, and shampoo twice. Coconut oil cuts protein loss and castor adds shine, but none of these oils grows hair; pumpkin seed oil's growth study used capsules taken by mouth. Grapeseed goes rancid fastest, so add the vitamin E and use within 6 months.

name: Overnight honey and Vaseline lip mask
claim: Softer, less flaky lips by morning
note: The fix for 'my balm wears off': a humectant under an occlusive. At bedtime, dab a thin layer of honey on slightly damp lips, wait a minute, then seal with petroleum jelly. Honey draws water in; Vaseline is the best-tested occlusive and stops it evaporating overnight. Wipe off any stickiness in the morning. Use daily until lips heal. Don't give honey to babies under 1.

name: 1:1:1 twist-up lip balm (beeswax, shea, jojoba)
claim: A firm tube balm that stays on for hours
note: Equal weights of beeswax, shea and jojoba make a balm firm enough for a twist-up tube. Melt in a water bath, take off the heat, stir in the vitamin E, and pour quickly into 4 or 5 tubes; it sets in 20 to 30 minutes. Wax gives staying power, shea softens, jojoba keeps it from feeling waxy. Peppermint is optional and can sting cracked lips, so leave it out if they're split. For very dry lips, use honey or a hydrating serum underneath, since a balm only seals in what's there.

name: Coconut coffee lip buffer (as posted)
note: As posted: fine coffee grounds and coconut oil, rubbed gently on the lips. Any plumping from caffeine is tiny and temporary; the smoothing is from the scrub. Use fine, dry grounds only, rub very lightly no more than once a week, and skip it on cracked lips. Keep water out of the jar. Brown sugar and honey is the gentler option.

name: Whipped cacao and herb body butter (like Indigo Elixirs Whipped Love)
claim: Rich, frosting-soft butter for dry, chapped or sun-parched skin
note: Indigo's list: cacao and shea butters, macadamia and sunflower oils infused with turmeric, lavender, rosemary, calendula and rose. Infuse the dried herbs in the oils on the lowest heat for 1 to 2 hours and strain through a coffee filter. Melt the butters, stir in the herbal oil, chill until just firm at the edges, then whip 5 minutes until fluffy. Water-free, so no preservative. Use a pinch of turmeric only; more stains skin and towels yellow. Melts in heat, so keep it cool.

name: Herbal all-purpose salve (like Indigo Elixirs Solve All Salve, comfrey-free)
claim: Soothing balm for dry, chapped, itchy or rough spots
note: Indigo's salve uses macadamia, sunflower and beeswax with turmeric, comfrey, lavender, lemon balm, oregano, calendula, spearmint and Hawaiian sandalwood. This version leaves out comfrey, because its alkaloids can be absorbed through broken skin, and the original is sold for cuts and scrapes. Infuse the herbs in the oils on the lowest heat 1 to 2 hours, strain well, melt in the beeswax and pour into tins. For dry, chapped, itchy or bitten skin. For a fresh cut, washing it and using plain petroleum jelly is what wound-care studies support. Not for cold sores (see a pharmacist) or inside the nose.

name: Sea buckthorn vanilla body balm (like Indigo Elixirs Seven Seeds)
claim: Golden, glowy balm for very dry or raw skin
note: Indigo's list: macadamia, unrefined sunflower, beeswax, cacao and shea butters, sea buckthorn berry oil and vanilla bean. Split the vanilla bean and warm it in the oils for an hour, then remove it. Melt in the beeswax and butters, stir in the sea buckthorn last, and pour into tins. Sea buckthorn is deep orange and can tint skin and fabric, so keep it at about 5%. Water-free; keeps about a year.

name: Enchanted rose roller (like Indigo Elixirs, safer swaps)
claim: Rose, spice and amber perfume oil
note: Indigo's list: macadamia and sunflower infused with cinnamon bark, rose absolute, patchouli, bergamot, black pepper, oakmoss and labdanum. Three swaps: bergamot FCF instead of regular bergamot (regular bergamot can burn skin in the sun); no oakmoss (one of the most common perfume allergens, tightly restricted in the EU); and benzoin-style warmth from vanilla instead of labdanum, which is hard to buy. Warm a cinnamon stick in the oils for an hour for the gentle spice, remove it, add the oils, and pour into roller bottles. Rest 2 days. Wrists and neck, not the face.

name: Jungle jasmine roller (like Indigo Elixirs)
claim: White-flower, vanilla and spice perfume oil
note: Indigo's list: macadamia and sunflower with vanilla bean, pikake (Jasminum sambac) and jasmine, sandalwood, cardamom, sweet orange and clove. Split a vanilla bean and steep it in the oils for a week (or warm an hour), then add the oils. Clove is strong and irritating, so just 1 drop. Rest 2 days before using.

name: Herbal scalp serum (like Indigo Elixirs Luscious Locks)
claim: Soothing scalp massage oil with rosemary and lavender
note: Indigo's list: macadamia and sunflower infused with rosemary, lavender, brahmi, gotu kola and sage, plus rosemary and lavender oils. Use dried herbs only. Warm the herbs in the oils on the lowest heat 1 to 2 hours, strain through a coffee filter, then add the essential oils. Massage a few drops into the scalp; leave in, or overnight and shampoo. The massage itself is the most proven part; herb growth claims are weak.

name: Rose citrus hair oil (like Indigo Elixirs, sun-safe)
claim: Shine and frizz control for dry, curly or thick hair
note: Indigo's list: macadamia and sunflower infused with rose petals, plus orange, bergamot, lime and cardamom oils. Regular bergamot and cold-pressed lime can cause burns or dark patches where oiled skin meets sun (scalp parting, hairline, neck), so this uses bergamot FCF and steam-distilled citrus. Infuse dried petals in the oils 1 to 2 hours on low, strain, add the oils. A few drops on wet or dry lengths.

name: Tulsi lime deodorant balm (like Indigo Elixirs, mild)
note: Indigo's list: macadamia, sunflower, beeswax, arrowroot, gotu kola, violet leaf, lime, benzoin, tulsi and cardamom. Infuse dried tulsi and gotu kola in the oils, strain, melt in the beeswax, stir in the arrowroot and oils, and pour into a tin or tube. Steam-distilled lime instead of cold-pressed (underarms see sun in summer). It's a mild deodorant, not an antiperspirant, so you'll still sweat; reapply as needed. Claims that violet leaf or gotu kola 'detox' or 'support lymph flow' aren't real; underarms don't hold toxins.

name: Turmeric black soap wash (like Indigo Elixirs Black ʻOlena)
claim: Gentle-feeling liquid wash for face, body and hair
note: Indigo's is turmeric hydrosol plus African black soap. Grate or shave the black soap and dissolve it in warm hydrosol, stir in glycerin, cool, and add Cosgard, since it now contains water. Black soap is real soap (pH about 9 to 10), so it can dry or sting sensitive and eczema-prone skin despite the 'healing' reputation; patch test and moisturise after. Not for eyes.

name: Five-oil hair growth blend (olive, rosemary, flax, coconut, castor)
claim: Softer, stronger hair from a weekly oiling
note: From a TikTok reply: olive, rosemary, flaxseed, coconut and castor oils. Mix and use as a pre-wash: massage into the scalp and lengths, leave 1 hour to overnight, shampoo twice. As she says, adjust to your hair: less castor and olive for fine or oily hair, more coconut for breakage. Flaxseed oil goes rancid fastest, so make small batches. Oils reduce breakage; they don't make hair grow faster.

name: Turmeric latte massage bar (like Lush)
note: Lush's Turmeric Latte reads more caramel-spice than plain vanilla. Vanilla, cardamom and a pinch of turmeric give that here; keep turmeric to a pinch, or it stains skin and towels yellow. Melt the beeswax and butters in a water bath, take off the heat, stir in the oils, cool slightly, add the scent and pour into a silicone mould (a muffin tin works). Sets in a few hours. To use: warm it between your hands or glide it over damp skin straight after a shower; it melts on contact. Store in a tin, dry and away from heat, so it doesn't melt or pick up lint. Water-free, so no preservative needed.

name: Coconut drench massage bar (like Lush)
claim: Rich vanilla-coconut bar for very dry skin
note: Lush's Coconut Drench is tonka, vanilla and coconut. Coconut oil softens the bar and adds the scent; vanilla stands in for tonka. Coconut oil melts at about 24 C, so this one is softest: keep it somewhere cool. Melt the beeswax and butters in a water bath, take off the heat, stir in the oils, cool slightly, add the scent and pour into a silicone mould (a muffin tin works). Sets in a few hours. To use: warm it between your hands or glide it over damp skin straight after a shower; it melts on contact. Store in a tin, dry and away from heat, so it doesn't melt or pick up lint. Water-free, so no preservative needed.

name: Cardamom orange massage bar (like Lush Hayl)
note: Lush's Hayl is cardamom and orange. Sweet orange is fine here; regular bergamot and lime aren't (they can burn skin in sun). Melt the beeswax and butters in a water bath, take off the heat, stir in the oils, cool slightly, add the scent and pour into a silicone mould (a muffin tin works). Sets in a few hours. To use: warm it between your hands or glide it over damp skin straight after a shower; it melts on contact. Store in a tin, dry and away from heat, so it doesn't melt or pick up lint. Water-free, so no preservative needed.

name: Rose jasmine shimmer massage bar (like Lush True Romance / Ro's Argan)
claim: Rose-scented bar that doubles as a solid perfume
note: Rose with a little jasmine for True Romance; add the mica for Ro's Argan shimmer. Argan oil is optional (almond works the same). Jasmine is strong and a known allergen, so keep it to 2 drops. Melt the beeswax and butters in a water bath, take off the heat, stir in the oils, cool slightly, add the scent and pour into a silicone mould (a muffin tin works). Sets in a few hours. To use: warm it between your hands or glide it over damp skin straight after a shower; it melts on contact. Store in a tin, dry and away from heat, so it doesn't melt or pick up lint. Water-free, so no preservative needed.

name: Lavender chamomile sleep bar (like Lush Deep Sleep, no magnesium)
note: Lush's Deep Sleep adds magnesium chloride. Magnesium salts don't dissolve in an oil bar and often itch, and there's no good evidence skin absorbs enough to help sleep, so this leaves it out. The lavender scent and the slow massage are what relax you. Melt the beeswax and butters in a water bath, take off the heat, stir in the oils, cool slightly, add the scent and pour into a silicone mould (a muffin tin works). Sets in a few hours. To use: warm it between your hands or glide it over damp skin straight after a shower; it melts on contact. Store in a tin, dry and away from heat, so it doesn't melt or pick up lint. Water-free, so no preservative needed.

name: Each Peach citrus massage bar (like Lush, sun-safe)
note: Lush's Each Peach is grapefruit, lime and orange. Cold-pressed grapefruit and lime can burn skin in sunlight in a leave-on bar, so this uses steam-distilled citrus plus sweet orange. Melt the beeswax and butters in a water bath, take off the heat, stir in the oils, cool slightly, add the scent and pour into a silicone mould. Glide over damp skin after a shower. Store in a tin, dry and away from heat. Water-free, so no preservative.

name: Cooling after-workout massage bar (like Lush After)
claim: Minty, cooling bar for sore muscles
note: Lush's After uses peppermint, spearmint and eucalyptus with magnesium. Menthol and mint feel cooling, which is what eases the 'ache' sensation; there's no good evidence magnesium soaks in through skin. Keep off the face, and away from children under 6 (mint and eucalyptus can affect their breathing). Melt the beeswax and butters in a water bath, take off the heat, stir in the oils, cool slightly, add the scent and pour into a silicone mould. Glide over damp skin after a shower. Store in a tin, dry and away from heat. Water-free, so no preservative.

name: Neroli lavender massage bar (like Lush Therapy)
claim: Light floral bar to wind down
note: Lush's Therapy is lavender and neroli. A gentle, calming scent; the 'improves tone and texture' claim comes from the butters moisturising, not the oils. Melt the beeswax and butters in a water bath, take off the heat, stir in the oils, cool slightly, add the scent and pour into a silicone mould. Glide over damp skin after a shower. Store in a tin, dry and away from heat. Water-free, so no preservative.

name: Unscented bump balm bar (like Lush The Bump, pregnancy-friendly)
claim: Rich, fragrance-free balm for a growing belly
note: No essential oils, the simplest choice in pregnancy. Moisturising keeps stretching skin comfortable and less itchy, but no cream or bar has been shown to prevent stretch marks; genetics matter most. Bump influencers with no marks are usually lucky, not using a magic product. Melt the beeswax and butters in a water bath, take off the heat, stir in the oils, cool slightly, add the scent and pour into a silicone mould. Glide over damp skin after a shower. Store in a tin, dry and away from heat. Water-free, so no preservative.

name: Almond shower oil (as posted, castile)
claim: Silky oil that turns milky as it lathers
note: As posted: grapeseed and avocado oils with Dr Bronner's almond castile soap. Castile and oil separate in the bottle, so shake well each time, and it lathers less than the 'milky' videos suggest. Keep water out of the bottle. Castile is alkaline (pH about 9), so it can feel drying on sensitive skin; for a true shower oil that turns milky, see the polysorbate version.

name: Milky shower oil (true shower oil, polysorbate 80)
claim: Oil that turns into a milky, rinse-clean lather with water
note: How store shower oils work: the polysorbate 80 lets the oil mix with water into a milk, (it lathers lightly, more like a milk than a foam). Stir everything together; no heating. Use on wet skin, massage, rinse. No water in the bottle, so no preservative, but keep the cap closed in the shower.

name: Body oil like L'Occitane Almond Supple Skin Oil
note: The TikTok mix: jojoba base, sweet almond, a little grapeseed, vitamin E and a touch of castor. Castor makes it thicker and stickier, so keep it small. L'Occitane's own oil is mostly almond and camelina with fragrance; for the marzipan-almond scent use a skin-safe almond fragrance oil, never bitter almond oil. Apply to damp skin.

name: Champagne rose bath oil (dispersing)
claim: Rose bath oil that disperses instead of floating
note: Polysorbate 80 makes the oil spread through the bath water instead of sitting on top (and making the tub slippery). Dried rose petals in the bottle look pretty but go mushy and brown in the tub, so strain them out or leave them on the side. Add a capful to running water. Rinse the tub after; oil can make it slippery.

name: Cold cream cleanser (like Queen Helene, gentler)
note: Queen Helene's Triple Whipped is mineral oil, water, beeswax, borax, SLS and fragrance with listed allergens. This is the classic cold cream with the SLS and fragrance left out. Heat the oil and beeswax, and the water separately, both to about 70 C, then pour water into oil while whisking. Cool below 40 C and add the Geogard (it contains water). Massage over dry skin, wipe off with a warm cloth.

name: Charcoal mascara (as posted)
note: As posted: coconut or argan oil, beeswax (or candelilla), castor oil and activated charcoal from capsules. Capsule charcoal isn't purified or tested for the eye area, and loose grains can flake into your eyes. Castor oil has no good evidence for lash growth; it just coats and darkens lashes. With no preservative, the wand carries bacteria back into the tube each time, so toss it after 4 weeks, or sooner if your eyes get red, and never share it.

name: Iron oxide mascara (safer)
claim: Black, buildable mascara that stays put
note: Uses black iron oxide, the pigment store mascaras use and that's approved for the eye area. Melt the waxes and oils in a water bath, take off the heat, stir in the pigment until smooth, and fill a clean, new mascara tube with a syringe. Wipe the wand before it goes back in. Toss after 4 weeks; never share. Stop if your eyes sting or itch.

name: Chamomile winter hand butter (as posted)
note: As posted: 100 g shea melted with 70 g chamomile-infused almond oil, chilled in the freezer about 30 minutes until the edges set, then whipped 3 to 5 minutes with blood orange and bergamot oils and vitamin E. At 2 drops in 170 g, the regular bergamot is under the safe limit for sun-exposed skin. If you add more for a stronger scent, switch to bergamot FCF (see the sun-safe version), because regular bergamot can leave dark patches or burns on hands in sunlight. Water-free, so the 6-month shelf life is fair if you keep water out of the jar.

name: Chamomile winter hand butter (sun-safe)
claim: Whipped, fast-sinking hand butter for cold months
note: Same method: melt shea with the chamomile oil, chill until the edges set, add the scent and vitamin E, then whip until fluffy. Bergamot FCF has the compound that burns in sunlight removed, so you can scent it more strongly. A spoon of arrowroot whipped in cuts the greasy feel so you can type afterwards. Use a clean, dry spoon to scoop.

name: Softer African black soap body wash
claim: Black soap that cleans without the tight, dry feel
note: Black soap is strongly alkaline. CAPB, glycerin, aloe and panthenol soften it, and a little shea adds richness. Grate the soap and dissolve it in the warm water, leave it overnight, then stir in the rest, adding the preservative last. It contains water, so the preservative is not optional. Kojic acid or kojic dipalmitate rinses off in a wash, so it won't do much for dark spots; put actives in a leave-on product instead.

name: Heavy cream hair butter (as posted)
note: As posted: blend heavy whipping cream with water about 3 minutes, strain and keep the butter, freeze portions, and apply every 1 to 2 weeks for 3 to 4 months. It's just homemade dairy butter. It can soften hair as a pre-wash mask, but there's no evidence it grows hair; growth and density are mostly genetics. It smells sour as it warms, so leave it on no more than 1 to 2 hours, then shampoo and condition. Fine or low-porosity hair can end up limp or stiff.

name: Shea pre-wash hair butter (keeps, no dairy)
claim: Rich pre-shampoo mask for dry, thick or coily hair
note: Does what the cream butter does, but keeps for months and won't go sour. Melt the shea, stir in the oils, chill until it starts to set at the edges, then whip. How to use: apply to dry hair, focusing on the ends, leave 30 minutes to 2 hours, then shampoo and condition as usual. For fine or low-porosity hair, use a thin layer or switch to a light oil such as argan.

name: Coconut water and aloe curl slime
note: Mix fresh coconut water with pure aloe gel and use it straight away as a light leave-in or curl refresher. Electrolytes don't hydrate hair; it's the water and aloe that help. Make only what you'll use today and throw away the rest, since it spoils fast and can turn sticky.

name: Fragrance-free lightweight body oil
claim: Feels like nothing, leaves a soft glow
note: Like the fragrance-free and lightweight picks (Neutrogena, Aveeno). Sunflower and squalane sink in quickly; jojoba adds slip. Massage 1 to 2 pumps into damp skin straight after a shower to lock in water. Good under perfume if you only want the perfume to show.

name: Thick body oil for very dry skin
note: Like the thick picks (Vaseline Cocoa, Palmer's gel oil). Avocado and castor give body and staying power, and a little melted cocoa butter adds that chocolatey richness. A little goes a long way; it can transfer onto clothes, so use it at night or wait 10 minutes before dressing.

name: Perfumed body oil (scent base)
note: Scent clings longer to moisturised skin than to dry skin, so a lightly scented oil under a matching perfume or mist helps it last. Keep the fragrance at about 1% (about 20 drops per 100 g) for body use, and do a patch test. Use a skin-safe fragrance oil, or build one in the scent builder.

name: East African herbal hair butter (kibe, as posted)
claim: Hydrating and moisturising butter for dry hair
note: Eritrean, Ethiopian and Sudanese style: unsalted butter is washed in cold water several times, then whipped with herbs and oils until pale and fluffy. Real benefit: it's a rich fat that softens dry hair and reduces breakage before washing. No evidence for growth or stopping hair fall. Keep it in the fridge and use within 2 weeks. Apply to dry hair, leave on 1 to 3 hours, then shampoo. On fine or low-porosity hair, a little goes a long way.

name: Herb-infused shea hair butter (kibe-style, keeps)
claim: Same rich, herby butter without dairy
note: Warm the oil with the dried herbs on very low heat for 1 hour (or steep 2 weeks), strain well, then melt with the shea, chill until the edges set, and whip. Plant butters don't sour, so it keeps for months. Use it the same way: on dry hair 1 to 3 hours before shampoo, or a fingertip amount on dry ends between washes.

name: Diluted vinegar hair rinse (after shampoo)
note: How vinegar actually helps: its mild acid flattens the hair cuticle after shampoo, so hair looks shinier and tangles less. Use it after shampooing, not instead of it. Dilute 1 tablespoon in a cup of water, pour over the lengths, wait a minute and rinse. Keep it out of your eyes. Don't use it neat; undiluted vinegar has caused scalp burns.

name: Homemade Vaseline alternative (as posted)
note: As posted: ½ cup jojoba or sweet almond oil with 2 tablespoons beeswax pellets, melted in a double boiler and cooled in a clean, dry jar. It's a soft salve, a good protective layer for lips, cuticles and dry patches. Petroleum jelly still seals in water better and is very safe; the oil-and-wax version just feels nicer and soaks in more. More beeswax makes it firmer.

name: Caffeine scalp tonic (like The Inkey List or Kundal)
claim: Lightweight scalp serum for thinning hair
note: The DIY version of the caffeine scalp serums. Dissolve the caffeine in warm water, add the rest, preservative last. Part your hair and drop it along the scalp, then massage 1 minute; don't rinse. Use daily for at least 3 months to judge. Caffeine has weak proof (lab studies and one industry-linked trial); minoxidil is the proven option if thinning is real. Keep it away from your eyes.

name: Niacinamide brightening body gel (leave-on)
claim: Evens tone more than a rinse-off brightening mask
note: Brightening masks you wash off after 10 minutes (lemon, lily and kojic, for example) have little time to work. Niacinamide at 4% left on the skin has the best proof for evening tone and is gentle. Dissolve the niacinamide and panthenol in the water, sprinkle in the xanthan and stir until it gels, then add the preservative. Smooth on after showering. Give it 8 to 12 weeks, and wear sunscreen on exposed areas or the spots come back.

name: Protein hair mask for damaged hair (like Elizavecca CER-100)
claim: Fills in damaged, porous hair for strength and shine
note: Protein treatments like CER-100 really do help bleached, coloured or heat-damaged hair: small proteins fill gaps in the hair so it breaks less, temporarily. Stir everything together and add the preservative last. Apply to clean, damp hair, leave 10 to 15 minutes, then rinse and follow with a moisturising conditioner. Once every 1 to 2 weeks; too often and low-porosity hair turns stiff and brittle.

name: Korean herbal scalp shampoo bar (like Saebom)
claim: Green herbal bar for a clean, balanced scalp
note: Saebom's bar lists ginseng, ginger, rosemary, he shou wu, reishi, sophora, woad, thuja, soap pod, black sesame, goji and mulberry with olive, coconut, shea and tea tree. This version keeps the gentle, useful ones and uses SCI, a mild cleanser made for hair, instead of true soap; soap is alkaline and can leave hair dull and tangly, especially in hard water.
